Uniform Title: Durgārcanapaddhati Author: Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa Gosvāmī

Description: This is a modern manual for the worship of the goddess Durgā. It was composed by Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa Gosvāmī, a Bengali Brāhmaṇa who served as professor at the Vidyādharmavardhinī Pāṭhaśālā Sanskrit College in Agra, where he taught the Yajurveda. He was also an expert in ritual practice. The manual was published in 1952 along with a commentary (*bhāṣāṭīkā*) by his son, Ghanaśyāma Gosvāmī.

The ritual is described in great detail, providing all the necessary particulars for its complete performance according to the instructions given in the text. This extensive rite is primarily performed during the period of Navarātri, usually in conjunction with the recitation of the *Durgāsaptasatī* extracted from the *Mārkaṇḍeyapurāṇa*. The layout is exceptionally clear and systematic, enabling anyone with a basic knowledge of ritual procedure and Sanskrit to perform the rites. Consequently, it has become a very popular work throughout North India.
Notes: Data entered by the staff of Muktabodha under the direction of Mark S. G. Dyczkowski. Revision 0: February 21, 2016.
Publisher: Ghanaśyāma Gosvāmī.
Year of publication: 1952. Country of publication: India.
Homage to Śrī Gaṇeśa!
Now, the procedure for the installation of the ritual pitcher (kalaśa) during the worship of Durgā:
He who, under the pretext of binding Bali, was employed by Hari to conquer Tripura along with Hara;
To create the world, he was born from the source of all disputants; as Śeṣa, he supports the earth with his hoods.

May that elephant-faced one protect us— he who was meditated upon by Pārvatī for the destruction of Mahiṣāsura, by the lords of the Siddhas for their spiritual perfection, and by the five-arrowed god for the conquest of the universe.

There, on the first lunar day (pratipad), having performed an auspicious bath with flower-essence oil and other substances in the forenoon—[as stated in the Rudrayāmala: "Having performed an auspicious bath, one should then worship the Goddess;
having first prepared an altar with pure clay"]—one should perform the daily rites (nityakriyā).
Having put on two new garments, having anointed all his limbs with sandalwood, musk, and saffron, and having applied either the *tripuṇḍra* or the *ūrdhvapuṇḍra*,
[one should perform the worship of the deity; in the worship, the east is in the middle for the worshiper and the object of worship].
O Goddess! Having assumed the Vīrāsana or other such postures, the practitioner of mantra should sit upon his seat and place the ritual substances before him.

One should offer perfumes, flowers, unbroken grains (akṣata), and so forth, as well as lamps on all sides; the food offering (naivedya) should be placed to the right, to the left, or in front, but never behind.
The ghee lamp should be on the right, while the oil lamp is on the left;
likewise, the incense should be on the left, in front, and never on the right.
One should offer fragrance, flowers, and ornaments in front;
everything else should be placed to one's right, and the *arghya* offering should be set down on the left.
One should place the offerings of food to be chewed, sucked, and so forth, along with other oblations, nearby;
one should designate a vessel at the back for the purpose of washing the hands.
Having diligently prepared all the materials for worship according to his own capacity, the practitioner should consecrate them with the root mantra.
One should display the dhenu-mudrā; this is declared to be the purification of the substances.
This applies to whatever is offered as naivedya and so forth, as well as whatever flowers, perfumes, and the like are used.
All the ritual actions must be performed while covered, until one invokes the Supreme Goddess.
The Rākṣasas accept their chosen deity, since they are without any covering.
(1) Having prepared a place of worship in the northeast direction of the shrine,

one should draw a circle, a square, an eight-petaled lotus, an eight-spoked wheel, a hexagon, a triangle, and a bindu upon the ground smeared with cow dung. Upon that, one should construct an altar (*vedi*) using clay from a sacred ford (*tīrtha*) or auspicious earth.

Having prepared barley or wheat, one should sow them. Nearby, having spread a white cloth upon a wooden seat and installed Gaṇeśa and the other deities, one should worship them. Afterwards, having established the water-pot (kalaśa) and worshipped Durgā, one should offer hymns of praise. On the ninth day, having performed the concluding worship of the deities installed [on the previous days], one should dismiss them.
The examination of barley sprouts as described in the Siddhāntaśekhara.
For the sake of the prosperity of the sacrificer, one should examine auspicious sprouts that have grown properly upwards, being tender and white.
One should avoid those that are smoke-colored, unprecedented, or moving crosswise; likewise, one should avoid those that are dark, humpbacked, and inauspicious.
The knowledge of the barley sprout and its fruit indicates that a lack of rain will occur; a black or smoke-colored sprout likewise portends strife,
while an incomplete or dark-green sprout foretells the destruction of people and famine.
If it is in the Tiryag-gati, there will be disease; likewise, if it is in Kubja, there is fear of enemies.
When an inauspicious sprout has arisen, one should perform a propitiatory fire-offering (śāntihoma);
the holder of the Guru’s form should offer oblations with the root mantra together with [the disciple].
With the Aghora-weapon or the Astra-weapon, one hundred or even a thousand times;
and by means of sprouts that have grown even on a *sarasvata* [tree], one should indicate the auspicious or inauspicious for the performer.
With dark or black sprouts there is loss of wealth; with those growing horizontally, disease; and with those that are swaying, the same.

If the barley sprouts are bent, there is suffering; if they are poorly grown, death; if they are crooked, disease; and if they are damaged at their base, loss of one's position, country, or desired objects.
The rule for planting the barley sprouts is seven days prior to the day of initiation (dīkṣā). By this, it is ensured that the day of initiation falls on the eighth day [from the planting].

It has been stated that "it must be performed. By the word "according to rule" (*vidhivat*), it is meant that one should know [the procedure] through the nine and the three [sections], as stated immediately before. This has been said in the *Siddhāntaśekhara*:
And likewise during the consecration, initiation, installation, and festival;
for the purpose of purification and peace, as well as at marriage and the tying of the sacred thread.
In all auspicious rites, one should perform the rite of sowing seeds (aṅkurārpaṇa) on the ninth or seventh day prior to the day of the consecration.
On either the fifth or the third day,
having performed the proclamation of the auspicious day (puṇyāha) together with the Brahmins, the preceptor (deśika) shall perform the offering of the ritual sprouts (aṅkura).
And on the day of the Maṅgalāṅkura sacrifice, one should perform it on the seventh or ninth day prior to the sacrificial rite itself.

In other tantras as well, during various festivals, in initiations, installations, and so forth, and in the rite of the sacred thread (pavitraka), that auspicious act performed by the officiant becomes auspicious when preceded by the specific ritual of the auspicious sprouts (maṅgalāṅkura). From the day of the auspicious conjunction...

"On the seventh day from now, or on an auspicious ninth day, or on the fifth—a propitious day at a favorable moment—one should perform the rite of the Auspicious Sprout (maṅgalāṅkura). Having fasted thereon the previous day and performed the Nāndī-śrāddha according to the procedure prescribed in one's own Gṛhya-sūtra, one should commence the offering of the sprouts. Thus it is said.

The preceptor must first be pure, having already purified himself on the first day; having made the formal resolve (saṃkalpa) and fasted, he should perform the auspicious rite of sowing the sprouts (aṅkurārpaṇa). On the preceding day, he should perform the Nāndīmukha Śrāddha and the recitation of the Svasti-vācana. All this should indeed be carried out according to the procedure prescribed in one's own Gṛhya-sūtra. Thus it is stated, and likewise in the Saṃhitā:

"In all cases, the performance of the *abhyudaya-śrāddha* produces the sprout [of success] for the rite whose nature is prosperity; this must be done at the very beginning. Thus says the *Havanakramasūtra*.
First, Gaṇeśvara is to be worshipped, followed by the syllable Oṃ in five ways;
then follows the sacrifice to the Gaṇas, the worship of Gaṇeśa, the Vāstu, and the Yoginīs.
The worship of the Mothers and the Mother-worship, the Vṛddhi-śrāddha thereafter,
the selection of the officiating priests (ṛtvij), and the Cakuśaṇḍikā rite according to the protective procedure.
The generation and installation are proclaimed first, followed by the vase;
then the invocation of the principal deity, worship, and the worship of the planets and other deities.
Immediately following that worship, there is the fire sacrifice (homa), the offering of oblations (balidāna),
the recitation of the Vedas after praising the planets, and the gratification of the twice-born (dvijātis).

Then follows the *pūrṇāhuti* (final oblation), the consecration (*abhiṣeka*), the circumambulation of the sacrifice (*yajñapradakṣiṇā*), and the ritual dismissal (*visarjana*); this is the sequence for the rite of pacification (*śānti*) proclaimed by Ghaṇaśyāma. Seated facing east or facing the Goddess, with hands holding ritual implements (*sopagraha*), having sipped water (*ācamya*): *Oṃ mūlaṃ bhūḥ ātmatattvāya*.
Namaḥ svāhā. || 1 || Oṃ mūlaṃ bhuvaḥ vidyātattvāya namaḥ svāhā. || 2 || Oṃ mūlaṃ svaḥ śivatattvāya namaḥ svāhā. || 3 || (And here the root mantra is: "O Durgā, O Durgā, O Protectress, svāhā!")
Oṃ. Whether impure or pure, or even if one has fallen into any state whatsoever,
whoever remembers the Lotus-Eyed One (Puṇḍarīkākṣa) becomes pure both externally and internally.

Oṃ. For the mantra "pṛthvi," Merupṛṣṭha is the seer (ṛṣi), Sutala is the meter (chandaḥ), Kūrma is the deity (devatā), and its application (viniyoga) is for sitting upon the seat. Oṃ. O Earth, by you the worlds are supported;
O Goddess, you are supported by Viṣṇu. Therefore, support me, O Goddess, and make this seat pure.
p. 4) Svastivācana:
Oṃ, salutations to the illustrious Mahāgaṇapati. Hariḥ Oṃ. Gaṇānāṃ tvā gaṇapatiṃ huṃ.
We invoke you, the beloved one; we invoke you, the lord of the beloved; we invoke you, the lord of treasures, O Vasu, my own.
I have conceived you as the bearer of the embryo; you, in turn, shall give birth to me as the bearer of the embryo. 1.
May Indra, of far-reaching fame, grant us well-being; may Pūṣan, the knower of all things, grant us well-being.
May Tārkṣya with his unbroken wheel grant us well-being; may Bṛhaspati grant us well-being. || 2 ||
Milk is on the earth, milk is in the plants; milk is in the sky, milk is in the mid-air; you are the givers of milk.
May the quarters of space be full of milk for me. || 3 ||
(5) You are the dominion of Viṣṇu; you are the dwelling-place of Viṣṇu; you are the needle of Viṣṇu; you are the fixed point of Viṣṇu.
Thou art Vaiṣṇava; for Viṣṇu, thee! || 4 ||

Agni is the deity; Vāta is the deity; Sūrya is the deity; Candramas is the deity; the Vasus are the deities; the Rudras are the deities; the Ādityas are the deities; the Maruts are the deities; the Viśvedevas are the deities; Bṛhaspati is the deity; Indra is the deity; Varuṇa is the deity. || 5 ||

Heaven is peace, the atmosphere is peace, the earth is peace, the waters are peace, the plants are peace, the trees are peace, the All-Gods are peace, the sacred word (Brahman) is peace, everything is peace; may peace itself be peace, may the Saman-chant be peace, may you be at peace. 6.
O divine Savitṛ, drive away all our misfortunes; send us that which is auspicious. 7.
O divine Savitṛ, they call this sacrifice for Bṛhaspati, the Brahman; protect the sacrifice with that, protect the lord of the sacrifice with that, and protect me with that. 8.
May the inspiration of the mind enjoy the clarified butter; may Bṛhaspati extend this sacrifice; may he establish this sacrifice as unimpaired. May all the gods rejoice here—Oṃ! 3! Be established! 9!
This sacrifice is indeed named "The Foundation" (Pratiṣṭhā); when they perform this sacrifice, everything becomes firmly established. || 10 ||
Oṃ! May there be peace, perfect peace; may there be the pacification of all misfortunes.
Oṃ! Sumukha, Ekadanta, Kapila, Gajakarṇaka, Lambodara, Vikaṭa, Vighnanāśa, and Vināyaka. || 11 ||
Dhūmraketu, Gaṇādhyakṣa, Bhālacandra, and Gajānana—whosoever should recite or even hear these twelve names. (12)
At the commencement of learning, at marriage, at entering or departing, as well as in battle and in times of distress, no obstacle shall arise for him. (13)
For the pacification of all obstacles, one should meditate upon the God who wears white garments, who is moon-colored, four-armed, and has a serene countenance.
Salutations to that Lord of the Gaṇas, who is worshipped by gods and asuras for the sake of accomplishing desired goals, and who removes all obstacles. || 15 ||
O auspicious one among all that is auspicious, O Śivā, accomplisher of all goals,
O refuge, O Tryambakā, O Gaurī, O Nārāyaṇī, salutations be unto you!
At all times and in all undertakings, there is no inauspiciousness for those in whose hearts dwells the Blessed Hari, the abode of auspiciousness. (17)
Blessed are they, victorious are they; how could there be defeat for those in whose hearts dwells Janārdana, dark as a blue lotus? 18.
Having first prostrated to Vināyaka, the Guru, Bhānu, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, and Sarasvatī, for the sake of accomplishing the purpose of the rite of pacification (śānti). || 19 ||
In all undertakings, may the three lords of the three worlds—
Brahmā, Īśāna, and Janārdana— grant us success.
O Vakratuṇḍa of massive body, with a radiance equal to ten million suns!
O God, always grant me freedom from obstacles in all my undertakings. 21.
Oṃ, salutation to the illustrious Lord of the Gaṇas, accompanied by Siddhi and Buddhi. Oṃ, salutation to Vāṇī and Hiraṇyagarbha. Oṃ, salutation to Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa.
p. 7) Oṃ, salutation to Umā and Maheśvara. Oṃ, salutation to Śacī and Purandara. Oṃ, salutation to the lotus feet of mother and father. Oṃ, salutation to the family deities. Oṃ.

Salutations to the chosen deities (*iṣṭadevatā*). Oṃ, salutations to the village deities (*grāmadevatā*). Oṃ, salutations to the local deities (*sthānadevatā*). Oṃ, salutations to the deities of the site (*vāstudevatā*). Oṃ, salutations to all the gods (*sarvadeva*). Oṃ, salutations to all the Brahmins (*sarvabrāhmaṇa*). Oṃ, salutations to all the sacred fords (*sarvatīrtha*). Oṃ.

Salutation to the illustrious Goddess Durgā, the foremost of whose deeds is this. Oṃ! May there be merit, may it be a meritorious day, and may there be long life. To the left: Guṃ, salutation to the Gurus. To the right: Bhaṃ, salutation to Bhadrakālī. Above: Gaṃ, salutation to Gaṇapati. In the heart: Duṃ, salutation to Durgā.
On the back: *Oṃ kṣāṃ kṣetrapālāya namaḥ*. *Oṃ, O sharp-fanged one of massive body, resembling the fire at the end of an aeon! Salutations to you, Bhairava; you should grant me permission.*
Oṃ, may there be well-being! By the command of the glorious Mukunda, who is existence, consciousness, and bliss, on this day—
the first day of the first fortnight of the first month in the fifty-first year of the current Brahmā’s second half-watch, during the second watch of the day, in the third muhūrta— may it proceed.
In the midst of the thirty-two kalpas beginning with the Rathantara, during the eighth, the Śrīśvetavārāha-kalpa;
in the midst of the Manvantaras beginning with Svāyaṃbhuva, during the seventh, the Vaivasvata-manvantara;
and in the midst of the four yugas known as Kṛta, Tretā, Dvāpara, and Kali, while the present one is occurring—

In the twenty-eighth Kali Yuga, during its first quarter, within the Jambūdvīpa situated among the seven islands inside the terrestrial mandala measuring fifty crores of yojanas in extent— and specifically within that [Jambūdvīpa], amidst its nine divisions, in the region extending nine thousand yojanas—

In Bharatakhaṇḍa, and there too in the most sacred Bhāratavarṣa, within Āryāvarta, in a portion of Brahmāvarta, in the field of Kumarikā, in the district of Mathurā [an adjacent district], in the field near Reṇukā [an adjacent field], Śrī...
On the western bank of the Gaṅgā and Yamunā, on the shore of the illustrious Narmadā—[in the year] numbered so-and-so elapsed from the reign of King Vikramāditya. (p.
In the current year, among the sixty-year cycle beginning with Prabhava,

in the year named [Name], in the [Name] solstice, in the [Name] zodiacal sign, in the [Name] season, in the [Name] month, in the [Name] fortnight, on the [Name] lunar day, on the [Name] weekday, in the [Name] yoga, and in the [Name] karaṇa.

When the Sun is in such-and-such a zodiacal sign, the Moon is in such-and-such a zodiacal sign, Jupiter is in such-and-such a zodiacal sign, and the remaining planets are situated in their respective zodiacal signs— as in this particular configuration of the planetary host— on this auspicious and meritorious lunar day, [I,] belonging to the such-and-such *gotra*...

For the sake of long life, abundant wealth, the unbroken increase of a lineage through sons and grandsons, stable prosperity, the attainment of fame, victory over enemies, and the fulfillment of all desired goals,
this [rite] has been performed on the first day of the Navarātri of autumn (or spring), with whatever materials have been made available.

I shall perform the installation of the water-pot (kalaśasthāpana), the worship of Durgā, the worship of the Kumārīs, and so forth. As a constituent part thereof, for the sake of ensuring completion without obstacles, I shall worship Gaṇapati, the five syllables (pañcākṣara), Vāstu, the sixty-four divine Yoginīs, the fifty Ajarās and others, the Kṣetrapālas, the seven Cirañjīvas, and the Seven Sages (Saptarṣis).

Following the installation and worship of the sixteen Mothers beginning with Gaurī, the pitcher of Varuṇa, the nine planets beginning with Sūrya, and their respective presiding deities (adhidevatās) and secondary presiding deities (pratyadhidevatās), one performs the installation and invocation of Durgā upon the wall, the installation of the water-pitcher (kalaśa), and the worship of Durgā upon it; or alternatively, [the sequence may differ].

Starting from the first lunar day (pratipadā) until the ninth, and likewise above the three joints (trivṛt), I shall maintain an unbroken lamp filled with sesame oil and provided with a cotton wick, either by myself or through a Brāhmaṇa.
Worship of Gaṇeśa in the southeast corner.
Oṃ! We invoke you, Gaṇapati, the lord of hosts, the seer among seers, the most renowned for his wisdom.
O Jyeṣṭharāja, Lord of the Brahmas, O Brahmaṇaspati! Hearing us with your protections, sit upon your seat. Om! O Heraṃba! Come, come, you son of Ambikā and Tryambaka!

O Lord of accomplishment and wisdom, three-eyed one, possessing a radiance equal to ten million suns; O serpent-faced one, adorned with a necklace of serpents, you who are the four-armed king of the Gaṇas; decorated with your divine weapons—the noose, the goad, and the battle-axe—I invoke you for the sake of worship and for my protection.
Of the sacrifice.
"Having come here, accept this worship and protect my sacrifice. Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ!
O Gaṇeśa, come here; stay here! Salutation to Gaṇapati; I invoke Gaṇapati."
I offer salutations; I present water for the feet at the feet; salutations.
I offer arghya to the two hands; obeisance. I offer water for sipping (ācamanīya) to the mouth;
obeisance. I offer bathing water (snānīya) to all the limbs; obeisance.
For the sake of the lower garment, the upper garment, and ornaments, I offer a saffron-colored thread along with unbroken grains (akṣata); obeisance.
I offer the sacred thread; obeisance. I apply the fragrant paste; obeisance.
I offer unbroken grains; obeisance. I offer flowers; obeisance. I offer sprouts of *dūrvā* grass; obeisance. I cause the incense to be smelled; obeisance. [The visible lamp:
the incense vessel or oil lamp on the left; the ghee lamp with a white wick.]

On the right, [I offer] a ghee lamp with a red wick, and on the left, a sesame oil lamp with a white wick. "I show [these]; homage! One should place unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*) into the incense and lamp vessels. Having washed both hands: "I offer the food offering (*naivedya*); homage! Having sprinkled [the offerings] with water.

Having covered [the offering] with fragrant flowers, one should consecrate it as nectar by means of the *dhenumudrā*, reciting: "I sprinkle you with Truth by means of Right" (*satyaṃ tvartena paripiñcāmi*)—or at evening, "I sprinkle you with Right by means of Truth" (*ṛtaṃ tvā satyena paripiñcāmi*).
Then, displaying the *grāsamudrā*, one should offer: *oṃ prāṇāya svāhā*—*oṃ apānāya svāhā*.

Oṃ, svāhā to Udāna; Oṃ, svāhā to Vyāna; Oṃ, svāhā to Samāna. In the center, I offer water for sipping (ācamanīya); obeisance. For the purpose of subsequent nourishment, I present a small portion of food offering (naivedya); obeisance. Again, I offer water for sipping; obeisance.

I offer fragrance for the purpose of massaging the hands; obeisance. I offer water for the purpose of washing the hands and for the purpose of rinsing the mouth; obeisance. I offer betel leaf together with areca nut, cardamom, cloves, and camphor for the purpose of purifying the mouth; obeisance.
I offer this sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) according to my ability; obeisance!

(1) For the deity, the incense burner or an oil lamp is on the left; a ghee lamp with a white wick is on the right, and a ghee lamp with a red wick is also on the left; an oil lamp with a white wick is also on the right.
Prayer.
Oṃ, salutations, repeated salutations to you, who are devoted to destroying the suffering of devotees, the Lord of Gaṇas, the Lord of all, the bestower of auspiciousness,
the Lord of the gods, the holder of knowledge, the one with a protruding belly, the dwarf,
and the one who grants boons to those who are gracious toward their devotees. || 1 ||
To Vighneśvara, the giver of boons, beloved by the gods, the pot-bellied one, the complete one, who acts for the welfare of the world.
O Gaṇanātha, son of Gaurī! Salutations, salutations to you, whose face is like that of an elephant and who is adorned with white serpents. || 2 ||
By this worship, may Mahāgaṇapati, together with Siddhi and Buddhi, along with his limbs and his retinue, be pleased.
Oṃ! May a Brāhmaṇa, endowed with Vedic splendor, be born in this land; may a Kṣatriya, a hero, a skilled archer, and a conqueror of fortresses, be born;

may a woman who is a wise counselor and a victorious chariot-warrior be born; may a heroic son, fit for assemblies and capable of youthful union, be born to this sacrificer. May Parjanya rain for us according to our every desire, and may the plants be fruitful.
May our acquisition and preservation of what we have been taught be accomplished. Om Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ! O Brahmā, come here from the east;
stay here. Salutation to Brahmā; I invoke and establish Brahmā;
salutation. Om Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ! O Gāyatrī, come here from the south; stay here. To Gāyatrī...

Salutation! I invoke Gāyatrī, I establish her; salutation! Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Govardhana, come hither from the west; stay here! Salutation to Govardhana! I invoke Govardhana, I establish him; salutation! Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! From the north...

O Earth, come here; stay here. Salutation to Earth! I invoke Earth; I establish her. Salutation! Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Lord of Sacrifice, come here; stay here. Salutation to the Lord of Sacrifice! I invoke the Lord of Sacrifice; I establish him. Salutation! Thus.
Having established [it].
As before, perform the worship with water for the feet (*pādya*) and other offerings:

*Oṃ, I bow to these five syllables— Brahmā and the goddess Gāyatrī, as well as Govardhanēśvara, Pṛthvī, and Yajñapati.* Through this worship, may they, along with their limbs (*sāṅga*), [be satisfied].
May the five Praṇavas, beginning with Brahma, together with their retinues, be pleased; salutations to them. Right there, near Gaṇeśa—(p.
Now, for the worship of the twelve Gaṇeśas beginning with Vakrā in the southeast corner:
Oṃ namaḥ gaṇebhyo gaṇapatibhyaśca vo namo namo vrātebhyo vrātapatibhyaśca vo namo.
Salutations to you, O Gṛtsas and Gṛtsapatis; salutations to you, O Virūpas and Viśvarūpas;
salutations! Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O hosts of the twelve forms beginning with Vakrā, come here, stay here! Salutations to the hosts of the twelve forms beginning with Vakrā.
I invoke and establish the Gaṇapas who abide in the twelve forms beginning with Vakrā; homage!
The worship with water for the feet and other offerings:

*Oṃ namo devagaṇeśāya*, salutations to you, O Destroyer of Obstacles! Salutations again and again to the one mounted upon a mouse, the performer of auspicious deeds! Salutations to the son of Kātyāyanī; salutations to the one who holds an axe in his hand!
O wise one, grant me the form of the rising sun; grant me beauty and prosperity;

grant me the abundance of sons. O God, bestower of the fulfillment of desires, may you always be as I have described. By this worship, may the twelve lords of the hosts, beginning with Vakra, together with their limbs and retinues, be pleased with me.
Now, in the southwest corner, the worship of Vāstu:
Oṃ, O Lord of the Dwelling (Vāstoṣpati), acknowledge us; be one who dwells within us, free from disease, for our sake.
Grant us what we seek; be auspicious to our bipeds and auspicious to our quadrupeds. Oṃ.
Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Vāstupuruṣa, come here; stay here. Homage to Vāstupuruṣa!
I invoke and establish Vāstupuruṣa; obeisance!

I bow to the deity Vāstudeva, the lord of Pātāla, who is mounted upon the back of a serpent, holds a trident in his hand, and possesses great strength. (Prayer for worship with water for the feet and other offerings.)
By this worship, may the deity Vāstu, together with his limbs and his retinue, be pleased; salutations to me.
Now, for the worship of the sixty-four Yoginīs beginning with Divyā in the northwest corner: Oṃ jātavedase sunavāma somaṃ rātīyato nidahāti vedah sa naḥ p.
Agni, like a protector, carries us across all difficulties; he carries us beyond all sins, as one crosses rivers. *Oṃ Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ*.
O sixty-four Yoginīs of the divine realm and others, come here! Stay here! Salutations to the sixty-four Yoginīs of the divine realm and others!
I invoke and establish the sixty-four Yoginīs of the divine realm and others; salutations!
Prayer for the worship with water for the feet and other offerings:
Oṃ! Victorious are all the Yoginīs; they are known to be the forms of Durgā.
May they always be satisfied with this worship and the offering of the bali.
By this worship, may the sixty-four Yoginīs, beginning with the Divine (Divya), together with their limbs and retinues, be pleased;
salutations to me!
Then, in the northwest corner near the Yoginī, is the worship of the fifty Kṣetrapālas beginning with Ajara:

Oṃ ajāre piśaṅgilā svāvitkuru piśaṅgilā śaśa... [etc. ... ihāgacchata iha tiṣṭhata. Homage to the Kṣetrapas beginning with Ajara. (Oṃ ajāre piśaṅgilā svāvitkuru piśaṅgilā śaśa... pañcāśatkṣetrapā ihāgacchata iha tiṣṭhata ajarādikṣetrapebhyo namaḥ).
I invoke and establish the field-protectors beginning with Ajarā; homage!
Prayer for the worship with water for the feet (*pādya*) and other offerings:

Oṃ, I pay homage to the *kṣetrapālas*, the destroyers of all misfortunes; for the sake of the success of this sacrifice, they have been worshipped by me. Through this worship, may they, together with their limbs and retinues, [be pleased].
May the fifty field-protectors, beginning with Aja, be pleased with me.
The worship of the sixteen Mātṛkās in the northern direction:
Oṃ *gaurīrmimāya salilāni takṣaty ekapadī dvipadī sā catuṣpadī aṣṭāpadī navapadī babhūvuṣī sahasrākṣarā parame vyoman*. Oṃ *bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ*.
O Gaurī and the other sixteen Mothers, come here; stay here. Salutations to Gaurī and the other sixteen Mothers. We invoke and establish Gaurī and the other Mothers; salutations.
Prayer for worship beginning with the water for the feet (pādya).
Oṃ! Gaurī, Padmā, Śacī, Medhā, Sāvitrī, Vijayā, Jayā, Devasenā, Svadhā, Svāhā, the Mothers, and the Mothers of the World.
Hṛṣṭi, Puṣṭi, and Tuṣṭi are the family deities (kuladevatā) of the self;
these sixteen, including Gaṇeśa as the preeminent one, are to be worshipped during the rite for prosperity (vṛddhi).
By this worship, may Gaurī and the other sixteen Mothers, together with their limbs and retinues, be pleased; [may it be] for my sake.

Vasoddhārā-pūjana: Oṃ, you are the purifier of wealth, with a hundred streams; you are the purifier of wealth, with a thousand streams. May the god Savitṛ purify you with the purifier of wealth, with a hundred streams, well-swept and dripping with sweetness. Having worshipped [the vessel] with perfumes and other offerings.
Śrī, Lakṣmī, Dhṛti, Medhā, Śraddhā, Prajñā, and Sarasvatī—
all these seven mothers of ghee have been worshipped with ghee.
O Vasoddhārā, O Mahāmāyā, O Cāmuṇḍā, O wearer of a garland of skulls!
Grant me my boon quickly; salutations to you, the supreme goal.
The *nāndī-śrāddha* performed through mental resolve follows the sequence from south to north.

Having proclaimed the place and time: "Today, as an ancillary to the sacrifice to Durgā, I shall perform the Nāndī-śrāddha according to the *saṃkalpa* rite, with gold [as the fee] according to my capacity, in lieu of the food sufficient for feeding a pair of Brāhmaṇas. Oṃ, the Viśvedevas known as Satya and Vasu.

O Nāndīmukhas, *oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ*, this is for you: water for the feet, water for washing the feet, and water for rinsing the feet; may there be prosperity (*vṛddhi*). Then: O [you who belong to] such-and-such lineage, our mothers, grandmothers, and great-grandmothers, O Nāndīmukhis, *oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ*, this is for you: water for the feet.

The washing of the feet (*pādāvanejana*), the rinsing of the feet (*pādaprakṣālana*), and the prosperity (*vṛddhi*). O [Name], we, the sons of our father, grandfather, and great-grandfather, the *nāndīmukha*s—*oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ*. This is for you:

the water for the feet (*pādya*), the washing of the feet (*pādāvanejana*), the rinsing of the feet (*pādaprakṣālana*), and the prosperity (*vṛddhi*). Second, [the same for] the [lineage of] the second *gotra*.

O our maternal grandfather, great-grandfather, and great-great-grandfather, together with your wives, Nāndīmukhas: Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! This is for you—the water for the feet (*pādya*), the water for washing the feet (*pādāvanejana*), and the water for rinsing the feet (*pādaprakṣālana*). May there be prosperity (*vṛddhi*)! Now, the offering of seats (*āsanadāna*): Oṃ Satyavasu...

For all the Viśvedevas, who are named and whose faces are joyful (nāndīmukha): *Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ*, this seat is a comfortable seat; *svāhā namaḥ*. Thus, one should offer three blades of *kuśa* grass, extending toward the south from all sides with their tips pointing eastward; the same applies everywhere. *Oṃ*, [grant] the moment (*kṣaṇa*) for the Nāndī-śrāddha.

Let it be performed. Oṃ, may you two obtain [this]; we two obtain [this]. Oṃ, for our mothers, grandmothers, and great-grandmothers of such-and-such lineage, who possess the joyful countenances (nāndīmukhī), Oṃ Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ, this seat, a comfortable seat, svāhā, namaḥ.

Oṃ! At this *nāndī-śrāddha*, may you two accept the invitation (*kṣaṇa*). May you both accept it; we two accept it. Oṃ! For our ancestors—father, grandfather, and great-grandfather—belonging to the [lineage of] such-and-such *gotra*...

Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ, this seat, a comfortable seat, for the Nāndīmukhas; svāhā, obeisance. Oṃ, in this Nāndī-śrāddha, may the two of you accept the invitation. Oṃ, so be it; may you both accept, and we two accept. [For] those of such-and-such lineage, our maternal grandfather and great-grandfather...

Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, this is the comfortable seat for the great paternal grandfathers together with their wives, the Nāndīmukhas; svāhā, obeisance. In this Nāndī Śrāddha, may you two accept the invitation. Oṃ, so be it; may you two accept, we two accept. Then—
The offering of perfumes and other articles: Oṃ, to the Viśvedevas known as Satyavasu, who are Nāndīmukha, Oṃ Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ—may this worship with perfumes and other articles be accomplished;
may there be prosperity! [To] those of such-and-such lineage, our mothers and grandmothers...

To the great-grandmothers, the Nāndīmukhīs: Oṃ Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ, may this worship with perfumes and other offerings be accomplished; may there be prosperity! To our fathers, grandfathers, and great-grandfathers of such-and-such lineage, the Nāndīmukhas: Oṃ...
Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! May this worship with perfumes and other offerings be accomplished; may there be prosperity, svāhā!

To our second-generation maternal grandfather, great-grandfather, and great-great-grandfather, together with their wives, the Nāndīmukhas: *Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ*, may this offering of perfume and other articles, *svāhā*, be perfected; may there be prosperity. Then, the feeding.

The giving of the price for the release [of the ancestors]: Oṃ. Today, to the Viśvedevas named Satya and Vasu, who are connected to the Nāndī-śrāddha of the three ancestors beginning with the father, the three ancestors beginning with the grandfather, and the three maternal ancestors beginning with the maternal grandfather—Oṃ Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ—this [is for] you, the pair of Brāhmaṇas.
May this food being offered, or the gold which is its equivalent, given in the form of nectar— svāhā!— result in prosperity.
Oṃ. Today, on this auspicious occasion, for the sake of my mother, paternal grandmother, and paternal great-grandmother, who are the Nāndīmukhīs of the [name] lineage:
Oṃ Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ! This food, sufficient for the meal of a pair of Brāhmaṇas, or whatever gold is being given as its substitute, is offered to you in the form of nectar (amṛta).
Svāhā! May there be prosperity. [Salutations to] the ancestors—father, grandfather, and great-grandfather of such-and-such lineage, who are of the Nāndīmukha type.

Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! This food, sufficient for the meal of a pair of Brāhmaṇas, or whatever gold given as its substitute, being offered to you—may it, in the form of nectar, result in the attainment of *svāhā* and the increase of prosperity. [To those of] such-and-such lineage: maternal grandfather, great maternal grandfather...

O elder paternal great-grandfathers, together with your wives, Nāndīmukhas: *oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ*, may this food—or whatever gold is given as a substitute for it—sufficient for the feeding of these pairs of Brāhmaṇas, being offered to you, become the form of nectar; *svāhā*. May it be accomplished.

Prosperity! The offering of water with milk. Om! May the Viśvedevas, known as Satyavasus, who are Nāndīmukhas, be pleased. [May] the mother, grandmother, and great-grandmother of such-and-such lineage, who are Nāndīmukhas;
and the father, grandfather, and great-grandfather of such-and-such lineage, who are Nāndīmukhas, [be pleased].

May the second-generation ancestors—the maternal grandfather, the great-grandfather, and the great-great-grandfather—along with their wives, who are Nāndīmukhas, be pleased. Then: *Oṃ svasti naḥ...* [recite] for the Viśvedevas known as Satyavasus, who are Nāndīmukhas, for the sake of that which has been performed.

For the sake of the perfection and establishment of the fruit of the Nāndī-śrāddha, I relinquish this sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), consisting of the purchase-price for grapes, emblic myrobalans, and barley roots, as an offering. Oṃ, to the mothers, grandmothers, and great-grandmothers of [Name] lineage, who are facing toward joy (nāndīmukhī), for that which has been performed... Oṃ, [Name]...
To the ancestors—the father, grandfather, and great-grandfather—of the Nāndīmukha lineage, for the rite performed...

Oṃ! To the maternal grandfather, great-grandfather, and great-great-grandfather of such-and-such lineage, together with their wives, for the sake of [the merit of] what has been performed... [The acceptance of blessings: May our lineage increase!
May our lineage increase! May our donors prosper! May our donors prosper! May our Vedas increase! May our Vedas increase!
May our lineage not diminish; may your lineage increase. May faith not depart from us;
may faith not depart from you. May there be much to give for us; may there be much to give for you.
May there be those who ask of us; may there be those who ask of you. May these blessings be realized as truth.
May these benedictions come true.
Oṃ, mother, grandmother, and likewise great-grandmother;
father, grandfather, and likewise great-grandfather. || 1 ||
May the maternal grandfather, his father, the great-grandfather on the mother’s side, and the others—
may these all be well-pleased and grant me auspiciousness. (2)

Whatever rite in this *nāndīśrāddha* has been deficient or excessive, may it all become complete through the word of the seated Brahmins and by the favor of the *nāndīmukha* ancestors; "May it be complete," say the Brahmins.
Thus concludes the procedure for the Sāṃkalpika Nāndī Śrāddha.
The selection of the preceptor and others.

Oṃ. From "Today... and so forth, as before: I, of such-and-such lineage and such-and-such name, in this rite of oblation to Durgā, choose you, of such-and-such lineage and such-and-such name, O Brāhmaṇa, with these materials for selection, to be the Ācārya. [The Ācārya replies: "I am chosen."
O Bṛhaspati, that which surpasses the enemy, which is worthy of praise, and which shines brilliantly among the people with splendor and wisdom.
"O Bṛhaspati, bestow wonderful wealth upon us, O wonder-worker, for you have granted it to the righteous and the born.
With this mantra from the *Bṛhaspate* hymn, one performs the worship, followed by the washing of the feet.
O best of the Pāṇḍavas, that fruit which is obtained by the gift of a tawny cow at Jyeṣṭha Puṣkara on the full moon of Kārtika is obtained by washing the feet of Brahmins.
Fragrance.
I invoke here that Śrī, who has fragrant doors, who is difficult to overcome, who is eternally nourished, who bestows abundance,
and who is the sovereign of all beings.
Unbroken grains; flower garlands; [the recitation of] "Śrīśca te"; the binding of the marriage bracelet.
Through the vow, one attains initiation. [The Prayer:]
O Lord, just as Bṛhaspati is the preceptor of Śakra and the other gods in heaven,
so may you be my preceptor in this sacrifice of mine.
"Perform the ritual action as prescribed. "As far as my knowledge extends, it is auspicious. Thus is the Brahmā-consecration and the prayer.
Just as the four-faced Brahmā, the Lord who upholds all the Vedas, was present, so may you, O best of the twice-born, become the Brahmā in this sacrifice of mine. *Oṃ.
Brahma, the knower, first revealed from the east, from the expanse of light, the beautiful, the ancient one; he, the foundation of the world, brought forth the sun.*
Worship with the mantra; everything is as before.
The ritual for protection.
One should place barley, kuśa grass, dūrvā grass, sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā), unbroken rice grains, and mustard seeds,
together with cow dung and curd, into a copper vessel.
Salutations to you, Goddess Śāradā, who dwells in Kashmir;
I seek refuge in you, grant me the gift of knowledge. (2)
Oṃ! Having paid homage to the Lord of the Gaṇas and having paid homage to the Grandfather (Brahmā),
I reverently salute Viṣṇu, Rudra, the Goddess Śrī, and Sarasvatī.
Having paid homage to Sthāna, Kṣetra, Dinanātha, Niśākara,
Dharaṇīgarbhasambhūta, Śaśiputra, and Bṛhaspati;
Having paid homage to Rāhu and Ketu— the great planets, the sons of the Sun and the preceptors of the Daityas— one should especially do so at the commencement of a sacrifice.
Having paid homage to the sage Garga, I shall relate to you all the deities beginning with Śakra, as well as the great sage Nārada, according to the accounts of the sages.
Having paid homage to the sage Vasiṣṭha, that tiger among sages, and to Vyāsa, the seer who is an expert in all the scriptures, the great sage Viśvāmitra— [proceeded].
May all these sages, who are preeminent in knowledge, and teachers whose wealth is asceticism,
protect my sacrifice after having been prostrated to by me.

This is the demon-slaying, spell-destroying [formula] belonging to Viṣṇu. I cast out this great spell which a stranger or a kinsman has buried for me; I cast out this great spell which one who is equal or one who is unequal has buried for me; I cast out this great spell which—me.
Whether it was buried by a kinsman or by a non-kinsman, that great sorcery (valaga) I dig up from here.
That which a co-born has buried for me, or a co-born, I cut out and dig up as witchcraft (utkṛtyā). 5 || 23 ||

I sprinkle you, O slayers of demons, destroyers of secret spells, belonging to Viṣṇu. I carry you, O slayers of demons, destroyers of secret spells, belonging to Viṣṇu. I strew you, O slayers of demons, destroyers of secret spells, belonging to Viṣṇu. I lay you down, O slayers of demons, destroyers of secret spells, belonging to Viṣṇu.

I pile you around, O you two who slay the Rakṣases, who destroy the Valagas; you belong to Viṣṇu; you are of Viṣṇu; you are of Viṣṇu. You are the portion of the Rakṣases. I cast out the Rakṣas! I lead the Rakṣas, evil, and darkness away. O Heaven and Earth, clothe yourselves in ghee;
O Vāyu, know [these] drops; may Agni enjoy the clarified butter, Svāhā! To that which is made with Svāhā, go upward to the Marut-host of the sky. 6 || 16 ||
The slayer of demons, the observer of all people, has slain the two Māyās at their place of origin; he has taken his seat upon the wooden trough (droṇa) as his dwelling. 26.26.
May Govinda protect [me] in the east; may he whose banner is Garuḍa protect in the southeast;
may Vārāha protect in the south; and may Nārasiṃha protect in the southwest.
Keśava shall protect the western quarter, Madhusūdana the northwestern; Śrīdhara shall protect the northern, and Gadādhara the northeastern.
May Govardhana protect [the world] above, and may Janārdana protect it below;
thus may Vāsudeva Janārdana protect [it] in the ten directions.
Śaṅkha protects the sacrificial fire on his back, and the excellent Padma is on his back as well;
Gadā guards his left side, and Sudarśana his right.
May Upendra protect Brahmā; may Vāmana protect the Ācārya;
may Acyuta protect the Ṛgveda, and Adhokṣaja protect the Yajurveda.
May Kṛṣṇa protect the Sāmaveda, and Mādhava protect the Atharvaveda;
as for those Brahmins who are observers, they too are protected by Rudra.
May the lotus-eyed Lord protect the sacrificer together with his wife;
and may Hari protect every place that is devoid of protection.
Protection should be performed with Vedic mantras and white mustard seeds;
therefore, a wise person should always provide protection with every possible effort.
Then, the binding of the protective thread upon the hand of the sacrificer.
Oṃ! You, the youngest, born of the swift [soma], protect the patrons; hear our songs.

"Protect this child with a focused mind! By that powerful king, the lord of the Dānavas of great strength who was bound by no one—that [power] I bind upon you; protect him, O immovable one, immovably! Thus is the ritual for protection.
Now, the declaration of the auspicious day (*puṇyāhavācana*). Regarding the ritual for the placement of the water jar (*kalaśa*):
after the placement of the jar, one should worship Varuṇa along with his limbs (*sāṅga*) and then perform the declaration of the auspicious day.
Having honored the Brahmins with perfumes, garlands, and other offerings, one should cause them to recite auspicious benedictions during religious rites,
festive ceremonies, battle, or upon witnessing a marvel.
The recitation for the declaration of an auspicious day (puṇyāhavācana) is prescribed for a Brāhmaṇa as a rite for the gods;
this very same rite, however, should be performed for a Kṣatriya or a Vaiśya without the syllable Om.
With his knees touching the ground, placing his hands— joined like lotus buds— at his head,
and holding a golden pitcher filled with water in his right hand,
[he said]: "By the long [lives of] the Nāgas, the rivers, the mountains, and the three steps of Viṣṇu, may there be long life."
By this authoritative rite, may there be an auspicious day and long life. The gods reside in the midst of the waters;
everything is established in the waters. May these waters, placed in the hands of the Brāhmaṇas, be auspicious. || 1 ||
May the waters be auspicious. May the waters be auspicious.
Lakṣmī dwells in flowers; Lakṣmī dwells in the lotus. May she dwell with me eternally, and may there be well-being for us. || 1 ||
May there be gladness! May there be gladness!
May my merit remain unimpaired, and may there be long life, fame, and strength;
whatever is conducive to welfare in the world, may that always be mine. (1)
May it be uninjured and free from harm! May it be uninjured and free from harm!
Having given perfumes and other offerings into the hands of the Brahmins.
Incense, which bestows offspring and nourishment, should be offered to the gods with devotion using the mantra: "gaṃdhadvārāṃ durāṃdharṣām. || 1 ||

May the perfumes protect you; may there be auspiciousness. May there be auspiciousness. May the flowers protect you; may there be well-being. May there be well-being. May the unbroken grains (akṣatas) protect you; may there be longevity. May there be longevity. May the betel leaves protect you; may there be sovereignty. May there be sovereignty. [May] the sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇās) [protect you].
May there be protection; may there be health. May there be health. May there be long life, well-being, peace, nourishment, and contentment—may all these be present.

May there be prosperity, fame, knowledge, discipline, wealth, many sons, health, and long life. Having placed the syllable *Oṃ* at the beginning— that by which all undertakings of Vedic study, sacrifices, rituals, and actions proceed auspiciously and splendidly— I [recite] the Ṛgveda and Yajurveda...
This benediction from the Sāmaveda and Atharvaveda, esteemed by many seers and authorized by you, I shall recite as a meritorious declaration of an auspicious day, being permitted by you.
Let it be spoken: [This is] a Yajus. Draviṇodas swells; offer the oblation, step forward!
From the office of the Neṣṭṛ, you are impelled by the Ṛtus. [Yajus: May Savitṛ impel you among those who impel;

may Agni impel you among the householders; may Soma impel you among the lords of the forest; may Bṛhaspati impel you among those of speech. [Yajus: Oṃ! Neither Rakṣases nor Piśācas can overcome that first-born power of the gods.
For this is indeed a *guṃ*. He who wears this golden *guṃ*, O descendant of Dakṣa, secures long life among the gods;
he secures long life among men. [Yajus]
O you of lofty vital power, born from the pressed soma, dwelling in heaven and taking hold of the earth—O fierce one, grant us mighty protection and great renown.

One should recite these auspicious verses on a holy day: "May the minds of all the Brahmins—distinguished by their vows, observances, austerity, Vedic study, sacrifices, compassion, self-restraint, and generosity—be composed. We are of composed mind. May you be gracious; may you be well-pleased."

We are [ready]. Then, taking water from the previously established pitcher into a copper vessel, one should perform the sprinkling upon the head of the patron with *dūrvā* grass: "May there be peace; may there be nourishment;
may there be contentment; may there be growth; may there be prosperity; may there be freedom from obstacles; may there be longevity; may there be health; may there be auspiciousness."
May there be auspiciousness; may there be success in action; may there be success in righteousness;
may there be success in the Vedas; may there be success in wealth and grain; may there be the attainment of all that is desired.
May there be the removal of the undesirable. On the ground.
Whatever sin, disease, inauspiciousness, or misfortune there may be, may it be warded off far away—at this worthy recipient.
Whatever is auspicious, may that be; may there be no obstacles to future actions.

May there be an ever-increasing prosperity day by day. May auspicious and beautiful rites succeed in progressive excellence. May there be the perfection of the lunar day, the *karaṇa*, the *muhūrta*, the asterism, the planets, and the ascendant.
May the presiding deities of the lunar day, the *karaṇa*, the *muhūrta*, the asterism, the planets, and the ascendant [be favorable].

May they be pleased! On this lunar day, with its specific *karana* and *muhurta*, together with the asterism, the planets, the *lagna*, and its presiding deity, may [the deities] be pleased! May Durga and Panchali be pleased! May the Vishvedevas, led by Agni, be pleased!
May the hosts of Maruts, led by Indra, be pleased. May the wives devoted to a single husband, led by Vasiṣṭha and led by Arundhatī, be pleased. May all the gods, led by Viṣṇu, be pleased.
May all the Vedas, led by Brahmā, be pleased. [May the gods] led by Āditya...
May all the planetary deities be pleased; may Brahmā and the Brāhmaṇas be pleased.

May Ambikā and Sarasvatī be pleased. May Śraddhā and Medhā be pleased. May the Blessed Kātyāyanī be pleased. May the Blessed Māheśvarī be pleased. May the Blessed Siddhi be pleased. May the Blessed Siddhikarī be pleased. May the two Blessed Lords, Vighna and Vināyaka, be pleased.

May all the family deities be pleased. May all the village deities be pleased. May all the chosen deities be pleased. On the ground: may those who hate the Veda be struck down; may those who are adversaries be struck down; may those who create obstacles be struck down; may the enemies meet with defeat.
May the terrible things be pacified; may the evils be pacified; may the calamities be pacified—at the worthy recipient.
May auspiciousness increase! May the waters be auspicious! May the seasons be auspicious! May the fires be auspicious! May the oblations be auspicious! May the plants be auspicious!
May the trees be auspicious. May the guests be auspicious. May day and night be auspicious for us. (This is a mantra from the Yajurveda Śākhā: Oṃ! May Parjanya rain according to our desire;
may the plants ripen with fruit; may our security and prosperity be established.
One should pour water into the full vessel.
May all the planets—Venus, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Saturn, Rāhu, Ketu, and the Moon—along with the Sun as their leader, be pleased. May the Blessed Lord Nārāyaṇa be pleased.
May the Blessed Lord Mahāsena be pleased. May whatever merit there is from this introductory invocation (puronuvākyā) be [for the benefit of all].
May whatever merit there is in the *yājyā* be mine; may whatever merit there is in the *vaṣaṭkāra* be mine.
May that merit which is gained at the rising of the sun in the morning be yours; may this merit, endowed with auspiciousness, be yours.
I shall cause the proclamation of the auspicious time for merit to be made. Let it be proclaimed.

May they proclaim for us that auspicious day (*puṇyāha*), which is equal to the merit of a Brahmā-day, which brings about the creation of the universe, which is eternally born from the tree of the Vedas. O Brāhmaṇas, may you all declare this auspicious day in my house, together with my family and retinue. Om, auspicious day! (Recite three times). [Yajurveda]
Oṃ! May the divine folk purify me; may those possessed of wisdom purify me with their mind.
May all beings purify themselves; O Jātavedas, purify me.

Whatever auspiciousness was performed of old when the Earth was raised up by the Ṛṣis, Siddhas, and Gandharvas—may they declare that auspiciousness to us. O Brāhmaṇas, may you declare auspiciousness in the home of me, along with my family and my attendants. Om.
Auspicious! 3. Yajus: Oṃ, so that I may speak this auspicious speech to the people.
To the Brahmin and the Kṣatriya, *guṃ*; to the Śūdra and the Ācārya, and to one's own Ācāraṇa, *ya*.

May I be dear to the gods as a giver of sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā) in this world; may this desire of mine be fulfilled, and may Upamāda bow down. Whatever prosperity was bestowed upon the ocean by Mahālakṣmī and the others—
"Please describe to us that prosperity which is complete and possesses such great power. O Brahmins, may you describe the prosperity within the home of myself, my family, and my attendants."
Oṃ, may it be successful! (3) Yajurveda: Oṃ, may there be well-being for the sacrifice;
that which is called non-destruction bestows merit and the increase of auspiciousness.
May those who are eternally dear to Vināyaka grant us well-being. O Brāhmaṇas, may you all pronounce blessings for me, along with my family and my retinue, within this house. Om, Svasti!
Yajus: Oṃ. May Indra, of far-reaching fame, grant us well-being;
may Pūṣan, the knower of all, grant us well-being.
May Tārkṣya, whose wheel-rims are unbroken, grant us well-being; may Bṛhaspati grant us well-being.
They speak thus regarding the son of Mṛkaṇḍu, as well as Dhruva and Lomaśa.

When Śrī Rāma, the son of the king, went to the wedding of Śiva and Gaurī.
"May that prosperity which resides in the house of the Giver of Wealth (Kubera) be in our home. O Brahmins, may you say:
'May prosperity be in the home of me and my family, along with our attendants. "Om, may there be prosperity. 3. Yajurveda: "Om, may we obtain the desire of the mind and the truth of speech."
May the lowing form of cattle, the essence of food, glory, and prosperity take refuge in me; svāhā!
He is Prajāpati, the guardian of the world, the Ordainer, Brahmā, and the king of the gods.

May the Blessed One, eternal and constant, protect us from all sides. May the Blessed Lord of Creatures be pleased. Yajus: Oṃ! O Prajāpati, none other than you has encompassed all these forms. Whatever desire we have in sacrificing to you, may that be ours; this one is the father of that one, and that one is the father of this one. *yaguṃ*.
May we be lords of riches; *guṃ* Svāhā! For the long-lived and well-faring sacrificer, [may there be] continuity.
May all blessings be granted by the officiating priests who have mastered the Vedas.
Just as there is well-being for the Lord of Gods, so may there be well-being in the house of the Guru.

As there is well-being in Ekaliṅga, so may there always be well-being for me. Oṃ, may there be well-being for the long-lived one. (3) [Yajurveda] Oṃ, may we find a path that leads to well-being, free from harm, and easy to traverse, by which one avoids all enemies and acquires wealth. [Yajurveda] Oṃ, O divine Savitṛ, drive away all difficulties.
Grant that which is auspicious; may the meanings of the mantras be fruitful, and may all desires be fulfilled.
May there be the destruction of the intellect of our enemies, and may there be the rise of our friends.
[May] the Ṛgveda, the Yajurveda, the Sāmaveda, and the Atharvaveda [prosper].
May they, stationed at the mouth of Brahmā, eternally strike down your enemies.
Those men who always receive unbroken grains from the hands of a Brahmin—for them, four things increase:
longevity, fame, glory, and strength. This applies likewise to one desiring long life, one desiring glory, and those desiring sons and grandsons.
May health, wealth, and all my desires be fulfilled for me.
May prosperity, luster, longevity, and health attend me; being resplendent, may I be exalted.
May there be grain, wealth, cattle, the gain of many sons, and a long life of a hundred years.
May there be well-being for you, may there be prosperity, may there be longevity, and may there be an increase in cows, horses, wealth, and grain.
May there be prosperity! May there be sovereignty! May there be well-being! May there be the destruction of enemies!
This is the procedure for the installation of the fire, preceded by the fivefold consecrations (*pañcasaṃskāra*).

Then, having cleared a square area on a vessel or a leveled ground that is free from grass, hair, gravel, and the like, using three *darbha* blades; having discarded those *kuśa* blades toward the northeast; and having smeared it with cow-dung water; [he should draw] a line from west to east with a piece of wood or the root of a *śruva* ladle.

Having scratched [the ground] three times to the measure of a span (prādeśa) in successive order—3; or, having removed the earth with the ring finger and thumb according to the sequence of scratching—3; having sprinkled it with water—3; then [the substance] situated in a vessel made of bell-metal or clay, covered by a second vessel of the same kind.

Having placed [the fire] outside the pit in the south-eastern direction, one should offer the portion belonging to the flesh-eaters (kravyādāṃśa) with the mantra: "Oṃ huḥ phaṭ svāhā. Then, with the mantra: "I place Agni at the forefront as my messenger; I invoke the bearer of oblations. O gods, sit here," he should establish the fire on the sacrificial mound (sthaṇḍila) or in the pit (kuṇḍa), facing himself, for the purpose of its protection.
Having performed some preliminary assignment, one should pour water and unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*) into the two vessels containing the fire. Then follows the worship of the fire:
*Oṃ, four are his horns, three are his feet, two are his heads, and seven are his hands.*
The great god has entered into mortals, O bull, who, though threefold, does not tremble out of fear.

Having thus established the fire: "Obeisance to the Fire named Varada" (in rites for peace), one should worship [the deity] outside in the north-west corner with perfumes, unbroken rice, and other offerings. *Oṃ! Born from the splendor of Rudra, having two heads, two nostrils, five eyes, four ears, and two feet.*

He has seven hands. || 1 || On the southern side he has four hands, and on the left side three hands. He holds the *sruc* and *sruva* ladles, the *śakti* spear, and a rosary (*akṣamālā*) in his right [hands]. || 2 || A water-pot (*tāmara*), a fan (*vyajana*), and a vessel of clarified butter (*ghṛtapātra*) are in his left [hands]. He is endowed with seven hands, has two faces, and seven tongues. || 3 || And on the right...

He has four faces and three tongues, with his face turned toward the north; he is known as the twelve-crore-formed, endowed with fifty-two kalās, marked by the utterances of Svāhā, Svadhā, and Vaṣaṭ, and has a ram for his vehicle.

Wearing red garlands and garments, seated upon a red lotus throne—him who is fierce and named Vahni, I invoke that Fire. O you of immeasurable luster, seven-rayed one, you are the mouth of all the gods.
Come, O Blessed Agni; be present at this sacrifice.
May devotion to Hari increase along with the expansion of one's lineage. May there be stable royal fortune during times of joy,
the accomplishment of many words through the grace of Śiva, and the destruction of enemies by the power of speech.
"The sound of the letter *da*, however, is the destruction of poverty. Thus ends the recitation for the auspicious day (*puṇyāhavācana*) as stated in the section on giving (*dānakhaṇḍa*).
I bow to Agni, the kindled fire, the knower of all beings, the consumer of oblations; to the golden-hued, blazing Anala, who is prosperous and whose faces are turned in every direction.
Oṃ, O Varuṇa, hear this my invocation today and be gracious to me; seeking your protection, I have called upon you. Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Varuṇa, come here, stay here; obeisance to Varuṇa.
I invoke Varuṇa; I establish him; obeisance!
The prayer: Oṃ, to the god Varuṇa, who holds the serpent-noose and has the crocodile as his vehicle.
I bow to the one whose form is the vital breath (prāṇa), resembling pure crystal;
to Varuṇa, the lord of the waters, who holds a noose in his hand. I invoke you to this sacrifice;
may you accept this worship. Through this worship, may the god Varuṇa, together with his limbs and his retinue, be pleased.
Homage!
Then, in the northeast corner, the worship of the nine planets beginning with the Sun: Oṃ, moving through the black space, bestowing immortality and sustenance.
The divine Savitṛ comes upon his golden chariot, beholding all the worlds. Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ!
O Sūrya and the other nine planets, come here, stay here! Salutations to Sūrya and the other nine planets!
I invoke and establish the nine planets, beginning with the Sun; homage!
Supplication.
Oṃ! Brahmā, the enemy of the Asuras (Viṣṇu), the destroyer of Tripura (Śiva), the Sun, the Moon, Mars, and Mercury.
May the Guru, Śukra, Śani, Rāhu, Ketu, and all the planets become bestowers of peace.

Oṃ, obeisance to the presiding deities beginning with Īśvara. Oṃ, Śiva, Gaurī, Skanda, Viṣṇu, Brahmā, Purandara, Yama, Kāla, and Citragupta—these are remembered as the presiding deities. Oṃ, obeisance to the secondary presiding deities beginning with Agni. Oṃ.
Agni, Āpa, Mahī, Viṣṇu, Indra, Indrāṇī, as well as Prajāpati and Bhujaṅga,
and Brahmā are the respective presiding deities (pratyadhidevatās).
Oṃ, homage to Gaṇeśa and the other five world-protectors. Oṃ, I bow to these five world-protectors: Vināyaka, Durgā, Vāyu, Ākāśa, and the two Aśvins. Oṃ.

Salutations to Indra and the other guardians of the ten directions. Oṃ: Indra, Agni, Yama, Nairṛta, Varuṇa, Vāyu, Kubera, Īśa, Brahmā, and Ananta are the lords of the directions. By this worship, may the Sun and the others, together with their limbs and retinues, be pleased; salutations to me.
Then, having established the principal water-pot,
there follows the touching of the ground:
*Oṃ bhūr asi bhūmir asi aditir asi viśvadhāyā viśvasya bhuvanasya dhartrī*.
Support the earth, O Earth; look upon the earth; do not abandon the earth. Or else:
May Heaven and Earth, O broad Earth, bedew this sacrifice.
"Fill us with nourishments!"—having thus touched the *bhṛmi* (the stirring-stick).

Then, having prepared a mound of earth for him, or else a house, one should sow barley there along with wheat. There, one should place a water-pot according to the prescribed rite and preceded by mantras:
"Oṃ, you are grain; satisfy the gods; for out-breath, for in-breath, for diffused breath."

May Savitṛ, the god with golden hands, receive you for long life with his flawless palm, as he extends a long-reaching cord of vitality. O Cakṣuṣpetva, you are the milk of the great ones. Or alternatively: *Oṃ*.
The plants hold a consultation together with King Soma: "O King, [favor] him for whom the Brāhmaṇa acts."
"We shall plow. Having said this, one should scatter barley or wheat.
In that interval, there is a specific substance for the jar according to the distinction of one's desire: one desiring merit (*dharma*) should throw ashes;

one desiring wealth (*dhana*), pearls; one desiring prosperity (*śrī*), a lotus; and likewise, one seeking sensual pleasure (*kāma*), yellow orpiment (*rocanā*). One desiring liberation (*mokṣa*) should place a cloth; one desiring victory (*jaya*), *aparājitā*; and for the purpose of eradication (*uccāṭana*), *vyāghrī*.
For the purpose of subjugation, the root of *śikhin*; for killing, *marīca*; and for delusion, *kaitava*.

One should cast *pārantī* into the interior of the jar for the purpose of attraction (ākarṣaṇa). Thus, one should cast these [substances] into the jar according to the specific rite to be performed. *Aparājitā* is well known as *baḍī* or *khiraiṭī*; *vyāghrī* is the small *kaṭerī*; *śikhimūlikā* is the peacock-feather plant (*morapaṅkhī*); and *kaitava* is the thorn-apple (*dhattūra*).
(p. 26) Now, for the installation of the water-pot (*kalaśa*):
*Oṃ ājighra kalaśam mahyā tvā viśantv indavaḥ punar ūrjā nivartasva sā naḥ*.
May the thousand-streamed, abundant, and milk-rich cow yield for me; may wealth enter me again. Or.
"He flows toward the pitcher and the quiver; he is sprinkled; he is magnified by hymns at the sacrifices. Having thus established the pitcher, [he continues].
The pouring of water:
*Oṃ varuṇasyottaṃbhanamasi varuṇasya skambhasarjanī stho varuṇasya ṛtasadanamasi*. [Fill it] with water from a sacred bathing place (*tīrtha*).

Oṃ, O Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Sarasvatī, Śutudrī, with the Marudvṛdhā, Paruṣṇī, Vitastā, Ārjīkīyā, and the great Sindhu, hear me along with the Āpas! Having thus filled [the vessel] with water from sacred fords (tīrtha).
The offering of fragrance into the jar:
Oṃ, [I worship] her whose door is fragrance, who is invincible, eternally nourishing, and bestowing prosperity.
"I invoke here Śrī, the sovereign of all beings. Thus, one should cast perfume into the water-pot (kalaśa).

Now, the addition of all medicinal herbs: *Kuṣṭha*, *māṃsī*, the two types of *haridrā*, *murā*, *śaileya*, *candana*, *vacā*, *campaka*, and *musta*—these ten are known as the "all-herbs" (*sarvoṣadhī*).
Oṃ! Those herbs which came forth in the three ages of old, prior to the gods...
"Manainu vabhrūṇām aha guṃ śataṃ dhāmāni sapta ca. Thus is the casting of all medicinal herbs.
Now, the offering of *dūrvā* grass:
*Oṃ kāṇḍātkāṇḍātprarohantī paruṣaḥparuṣaspari | evā no dūrve pratanu sahasreṇa śatena ca ||* Thus ends the offering of *dūrvā*.
Now, the casting of the *kuśa* grass:

*Oṃ pavitrestho vaiṣṇavyau saviturvaḥ prasave 'punāmyacchidreṇa pavitreṇa sūryasya raśmibhiḥ | tasya te pavitrapate pavitrapūtasya yatkāmaḥ...* [Oṃ] You two are purifiers belonging to Viṣṇu; at the impulse of Savitṛ, I purify you with a flawless purifier, with the rays of the sun. O Lord of the Purifier, of that which is purified by your purifier, whatever my desire [may be...]
"May I be able to do this again"—thus is the casting of the clod.
p.

27) Now, the casting of the seven types of earth: Having brought earth from an elephant, a horse, a chariot, an anthill, a confluence of rivers, a lake, and a cow-pen, one should cast it into the jars; likewise from a crossroads. Thus, up to the cow-pen, there are seven.
[Together with the four, there should be eight.
*Oṃ syonā pṛthivī no bhavānṛkṣarā niveśanī | yacchā naḥ śarma saprathāḥ* — thus is the casting of the seventh earth.
Now, the offering of *puṅgī* fruit: Oṃ, those that bear fruit, those that are fruitless, those that are flowerless, and those that are flowering.
"May they, impelled by Bṛhaspati, release us from sin. Thus is the casting of the Puṅgī fruit.
Now, the casting of the five jewels: [Gold, the thunderbolt [diamond], sapphire, ruby, and pearl—these are the five jewels taught by those who know the science of gems.
Oṃ! Agni, the lord of wandering mendicants, the seer, has stepped forth toward the oblations; bestowing jewels upon the donor. Vāṭ!
"May Savitṛ, the Lord of Fortune, bestow jewels and treasures upon us; we pray for that wonderful portion.
Thus is the casting of the five jewels.
The casting of the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā):
Oṃ. In the beginning, Hiraṇyagarbha arose; once born, he was the sole lord of all that exists.
"The earth and heaven are the eternal support; to which god shall we offer worship with our oblation?
Thus is the casting of the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*).

Now, the addition of the five sprouts [according to the Brāhma]: "The sprouts of the *aśvattha*, *udumbara*, *plakṣa*, *cūta*, and *nyagrodha* are known as the 'five twigs' (*pañcabhaṅga*); they are auspicious for all rites. (1)
"Oṃ! On the Aśvattha tree is your seat; on its leaf is your dwelling made. You shall indeed be sharers of cattle, for you shall win back the man. With this, five sprouts are cast in.
Now, the binding of the safflower-colored thread:
*Oṃ yuvā suvāsāḥ parivīta āgāt sa u śreyān bhavati jāyamānaḥ*.
The wise poets, seeking the gods with their minds, draw him upward as they strive for perfection.
Thus is the binding with safflower-colored thread.
28) Now, the placing of a vessel full of rice upon the water-pot:
*Oṃ pūrṇād arviḥ parāpata supūrṇā punar āpata | vasneva vikrīṇāvahā iṣam ūrjam*.
"mūrjaguṃ śatakrato"—with this mantra, place a vessel filled with rice upon the water-pot (kalaśa).
Now, the Śrī-pahala-nidhāna: Oṃ! May Śrī and Lakṣmī be your two wives; may Day and Night be your two sides; may the constellations be your form;
may the Aśvins be your gaping mouth. Bestowing, bestow upon me; bestow upon all the world.
Then, having worshipped Varuṇa with the mantra: "Oṃ tat tvā yāmi brahmaṇā vandamānas tad āśāste yajamāno havirbhiḥ."
O Varuṇa, being unprovoked, do not steal away the wide-striding one who brings the oblation, he who shares the same life-span as you.
Having thus worshipped Varuṇa with water for the feet and other offerings, the prayer is as follows:
*Oṃ, Viṣṇu is at the mouth of the jar; Rudra is seated at its neck.*
Brahmā is situated at its base, and the hosts of Mothers are said to be in the middle.
Within his belly were the seven oceans and the earth with its seven continents;
likewise, the Ṛgveda, Yajurveda, Sāmaveda, and Atharvaveda.
All [the goddesses], together with their limbs (aṅgas), have taken refuge in the water-jar;
here Gāyatrī, Sāvitrī, Śānti, and Puṣṭikarī are ever present.
May all the oceans, rivers, sacred fords, clouds, and streams come to the house of the sacrificer (and mine), bringing about the destruction of misfortune. (4)
May they come to the house of the sacrificer— and to mine as well—
to destroy all misfortune, for the sake of the city of the gods, while the great ocean was being churned in the conflict between the gods and the Dānavas. || 5 ||
Then you were born as Kumbha, personally sustained by Viṣṇu himself;
all sacred fords are in your water, and all the gods reside within you.
In you all beings abide; in you the vital breaths are established.
You alone are Śiva himself, you are Viṣṇu, and you are Prajāpati.
The Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, Viśvedevas, and those belonging to the ancestors—
all of them abide in you, since they are the bestowers of the fruits of one's desires. (8)
"O Lotus-born One! By your grace, I desire to perform this sacrifice.
O God! Grant me your presence; be forever gracious."

Oṃ! O you who hold a noose in your hand, salutations to you, O life-giver of the lotus-born goddess! Remain present here until the principal worship is completed. Thus ends the worship of the water-pot (kalaśa).
Now, the Tantric protection:

Oṃ! Sūrya, Soma, Yama, Kāla, the two twilights, the spirits, the days and nights, the wind, the lord of the quarters, the earth, space, the sky-dwellers, and the immortals—abiding by the command of Brahmā.
"Imagine here a storehouse [of provisions]. Having touched the ground with these words, one should perform the binding of the directions.
The installation of the general *argha* pitcher:

[Regarding the proportions of the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*), the Vasiṣṭha Saṃhitā states: "Cow urine, cow dung, milk, curd, clarified butter, and water with *kuśa* grass—this is declared to be the *pañcagavya*, which destroys even the greatest sins."
One should provide cow dung with double the amount of urine, milk with four times the amount,
ghee with eight times the amount, and likewise curd for the *pañcagavya* [mixture].
The method for mixing the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*):

Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ | *Tatsaviturvareṇyaṃ bhargo devasya dhīmahi dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt* | [This is for] the cow’s urine. Oṃ *Gandhadvārāṃ durādharṣāṃ nityapuṣṭāṃ karīṣiṇīm* | [This is for] the cow dung.
I invoke here Śrī, the sovereign lady of all beings, O Govara. Oṃ, swell with strength on every side, O Soma; let virility be yours; be present at the gathering of nourishment. O Dūdha.
Oṃ! I have offered praise to Dadhikrāvan, the victorious, the swift, the prize-winning steed.
May that which makes the mouth fragrant protect our life. [Offering of] curd:
*Oṃ*, you are splendor, you are pure, you are immortality, you are the abode by name; you are dear to the gods, unassailable, the place of sacrifice for the gods. [Offering of] ghee.
"Oṃ, by the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan.
[Saying this,] having visualized a rampart of fire with a stream of water—*om raṃ*—one should begin the worship.
There, having established the common *kalaśa* and worshipped Varuṇa, one should perform the worship of the pedestal (*pīṭha*).

On one's own left side, having fashioned a mandala consisting of a dot (bindu), a triangle, a circle, and a square, and having worshipped it with "Oṃ Hrīṃ, obeisance to the Support-Energy (Ādhāraśakti)," one should place the support-vessel (ādhāra) there. [Then follows] the six-limbed [rite].

One should perform the worship. Having washed the vessel with "Oṃ kraḥ, to the weapon, phaṭ," and having filled it with water with "Oṃ krāṃ, to the heart, namaḥ," [one should offer] "Maṃ, obeisance to the fire-maṇḍala consisting of ten digits. "Oṃ aṃ, obeisance to the sun-maṇḍala consisting of twelve digits."
One should fill [the vessel] with water from sacred sites while reciting the root mantra. Having worshipped it again with perfumes and other offerings, one should say:
"Oṃ, salutation to the lunar mandala consisting of sixteen digits. O Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Godāvarī, Sarasvatī, Narmadā, Sindhu, and Kāverī, please be present in these waters."

With the goad mudrā [aiṃ hrīṃ klīṃ cāmuṇḍāyai vicce vā durge durge rakṣiṇi svāhā || 1 || Having made the middle finger straight and joining the index finger at its middle joint, one should bend it slightly;
this is known as the goad mudrā]. Summoning the holy fords (tīrthas).

Having recited the root mantra eight times, [one should display] the Dhenu (Cow) and Yoni mudrās. [As for the Dhenu mudrā: One should place the fingers of the right hand between those of the left; having joined the right index finger with the middle finger of the left, one should likewise join the left index finger with the middle finger of the right. Then, one should join the left ring finger with the right [index finger].
One should join the little fingers; this downward-facing, covered gesture is proclaimed as the *dhenu-mudrā*.

The *matsya-mudrā* is described thus: having placed the left hand upon top, one should extend the right hand; with the thumbs joined at their sides, this is called the *matsya-mudrā*. The *kumbha-mudrā* is formed with both hands.

Having displayed the *mudrās*—the *sāvakāśika*, *muṣṭikaraṇa*, and *kumbha*—and having sprinkled oneself and the materials for worship with that water, [this is] the general procedure for the installation of the *argha* jar. (p.
Oṃ, O Jātavedas, bring to me Lakṣmī—golden-hued, tawny, golden, wearing a silver garland, moon-like, and made of gold. [Recite] at the head.
Oṃ, O Jātavedas, bring to me that Lakṣmī who leads the way;
through her may I find gold, cattle, horses, and men. (For the two eyes.)
Oṃ, I invoke the goddess Śrī, who is borne upon a chariot drawn by horses, who awakens with the trumpeting of elephants; may the goddess Śrī be pleased with me. [Recite this] over the two ears.
Oṃ! Her smile like bell-metal, with a golden rampart, moist, blazing, satisfied, and satisfying others;
seated upon a lotus, possessing the luster of a lotus—her, Śrī, I invoke here. [To the two nostrils.]
Oṃ! I go for refuge to that lotus-faced Śrī, who is moon-like, radiant, blazing with glory, and honored by the gods in the world; may misfortune perish, I choose you as my refuge. [5] [In the mouth.]
Oṃ, O you who possess the splendor of the sun, born from austerity, the lord of the forest is your tree, the Bilva;
may its fruits, through austerity, drive away my misfortunes—both internal obstacles and external ill-fortune. (6) On the neck:
Oṃ, may the divine friend approach me, along with fame and this jewel.
I have appeared in this kingdom; may I bestow upon it flourishing fame. (This is for the two hands.)
Oṃ, I destroy hunger, thirst, impurity, Jyeṣṭhā, and Alakṣmī; I drive away misfortune and all lack of prosperity from this house. [Hṛdaya-mantra]
Oṃ, I invoke here Śrī, who has the fragrance as her door, who is invincible, eternally nourishing, bestowing prosperity,
and the sovereign of all beings— at the navel.
Oṃ! May we obtain the desire of the mind and the intention of speech;
may the form of cattle, the essence of food, prosperity, and glory rest within me. (In the Liṅga.)
Oṃ, from the mud all creatures were born; O Mud, arise within me!
Cause Śrī, the mother who wears a garland of lotuses, to dwell in my family. [At the anus.]
Oṃ! May the waters flow forth, making everything smooth; clothe me in my home.
O Goddess Śrī, the Mother, dwell within the depths of my family. [Place it] upon the thighs.
Oṃ, O Jātavedas, bring to me Lakṣmī— Ārdrā, Puṣkariṇī, Puṣṭi, Piṅgalā, Padmamālinī, Candrā, and Hiraṇmayī— at the two knees.
Oṃ, O Jātavedas, bring to me from Ardrā the golden staff, adorned with a golden garland, the sun-like, golden Lakṣmī. (Recite this) over the two shanks.
Oṃ! O Jātavedas, bring to me that Lakṣmī who never departs, through whom I may obtain abundant gold, cattle, female slaves, horses, and male servants. (15)
At the two feet.

Oṃ! He who, having become pure and restrained, should offer clarified butter daily, and he who desires prosperity should constantly recite this hymn of fifteen verses, [placing it] upon all his limbs. 16. Sarvāṅge.
Then, having placed a golden image of Śrī Durgā upon the water-pot (kalaśa) after performing the rite of fire-transference (agnyuttāraṇa),

and having covered it with silk cloths, one should worship it with the Puruṣasūkta, the Śrīsūkta, or according to the method prescribed in the Purāṇas, using either the sixteen-fold offerings (ṣoḍaśopacāra) or as many offerings as are available. It is as follows:
Now follows the procedure for the removal of the sacred fire.

In this regard, the preceptor, acting as the patron (*yajamāna*), having proclaimed the place and time, shall say: "For the purpose of removing defects such as those arising from the fashioning of this golden image of Śrī Durgā, I shall perform the installation of the vital breath (*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*) preceded by the rite of *agnyuttāraṇa*. Having anointed the image with clarified butter, [he shall pour] milk upon it.
One should cause a mixed stream of water to flow, or one should pour it down.
The mantras for the removal of the fire.
Oṃ! With the girdle of the ocean, O Agni, we encircle you; be purifying, auspicious, and gracious toward us. 1.
Oṃ! We envelop you with the womb of snow, O Agni; as a purifier, be auspicious and kind toward us. 2.
Oṃ! Coming from the waters, O reed, come from the rivers of the wind;
O Agni, we are your bile; come with the female frogs, and having come, O purifying one, make this sacrifice auspicious for us. 3.
Oṃ, this is the gathering place of the waters, the dwelling of the ocean.
May your missiles strike others than us; O purifier, be auspicious toward us. 4.
Oṃ! O Agni, the purifier, with your radiant and powerful tongue, O divine one, bring the gods here and worship them. 5.
Oṃ! O purifying Agni, bring the gods here for us; come to our sacrifice and to our oblation. 6.
Oṃ! O Purifier, he who has shone forth with the light of his splendor, like the dawn with its radiance;
advancing, he has surpassed the impetuous might of the archer, burning with his iron-like heat, insatiable and undecaying. 7.
