*Śaktibhyo namaḥ*—*Oṃ*, at the two feet. *Oṃ aṃ kṣaṃ kīlakāya namaḥ aḥ*, on all limbs. This is the *ṛṣyādinyāsa*. *Oṃ aṃ kaṃ 5 āṃ*, to the two thumbs, *namaḥ* to the heart. *Oṃ i caṃ 5 īṃ*, to the two index fingers, *svāhā* to the head.

Oṃ uṃ ṭaṃ 5 ūṃ, to the two middle fingers, vaṣaṭ to the *śikhā* (crest). O eṃ taṃ 5 aiṃ, to the two ring fingers, hūṃ to the *kavaca* (armor). Oṃ oṃ paṃ 5 auṃ, to the two little fingers, [vaṣaṭ] to the *netra* (eyes).
Trayāya vauṣaṭ. Oṃ aṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ laṃ kṣaṃ aḥ, to the palms and backs of the hands, astrāya phaṭ.
Meditative absorption.

Śiva, the Lord of Speech, should be meditated upon as holding a deer-tail fan and a rosary in His hands, and bearing a radiant garland of knowledge in His [other] hand. Then, one should perform the external *mātṛkā-nyāsa*:
*Oṃ Aṃ Namaḥ* on the head; *Oṃ Āṃ Namaḥ* on the face; *Oṃ Iṃ Namaḥ* on the right [eye].

To the eyes: Oṃ Īṃ, salutation to the left eye. Oṃ Uṃ, salutation to the right ear. Oṃ Ūṃ, salutation to the left ear. Oṃ Ṛṃ, salutation to the right nostril. Oṃ Ṝṃ, salutation to the left nostril. Oṃ Ḷṃ, salutation to the right cheek. Oṃ Ḹ, salutation to the left [cheek].

On the cheek: *Oṃ eṃ namaḥ*. On the upper lip: *Oṃ aiṃ namaḥ*. On the lower lip: *Oṃ oṃ namaḥ*. On the upper row of teeth: *Oṃ auṃ namaḥ*. On the lower row of teeth: *Oṃ aṃ namaḥ*. On the crown of the head: *Oṃ aḥ namaḥ*. On the circumference of the mouth: *Oṃ kaṃ namaḥ*. On the right [side]: *Oṃ kaṃ namaḥ*.

At the base of the right arm: Oṃ Khaṃ, salutation to the right elbow; Gaṃ, salutation to the right wrist; Oṃ Ghaṃ, salutation to the base of the fingers of the right hand; Oṃ Ṅaṃ, salutation to the tips of the fingers of the right hand; Oṃ Caṃ, salutation to the base of the left arm; Oṃ Chaṃ, salutation to the left elbow; Oṃ Jaṃ, salutation to... [the left wrist].

Oṃ *jhaṃ* namaḥ to the left wrist; Oṃ *ñaṃ* namaḥ to the base of the fingers of the left hand; Oṃ *ñāṃ* namaḥ to the tips of the fingers of the left hand; Oṃ *ṭaṃ* namaḥ to the base of the right foot; Oṃ *ṭhaṃ* namaḥ to the right knee;
Oṃ *ḍaṃ* namaḥ to the right ankle; Oṃ *ḍhaṃ* namaḥ to the [right]...

At the base of the toes of the right foot: Oṃ ṇaṃ namaḥ. At the tips of the toes of the right foot: Oṃ taṃ namaḥ. At the base of the left foot: Oṃ thaṃ namaḥ. At the left knee: Oṃ daṃ namaḥ. At the left ankle: Oṃ dhaṃ namaḥ.
Oṃ dhaṃ namaḥ at the base of the toes of the left foot. Oṃ naṃ namaḥ at the tips of the toes of the left foot.

Oṃ Paṃ, homage to the right side. Oṃ Phaṃ, homage to the left side. Oṃ Baṃ, homage to the back. Oṃ Bhaṃ, homage to the navel. Oṃ Maṃ, homage to the belly. Oṃ Yaṃ, homage to the skin-element in the heart. Oṃ Raṃ, homage to the blood-element in the right shoulder.
On the right shoulder: Oṃ Laṃ, obeisance to the one whose nature is flesh; on the hump: obeisance.
p. 109) Oṃ vaṃ, homage to the self consisting of fat; on the left shoulder. Oṃ śaṃ, homage to the self consisting of bone;
from the heart to the end of the right hand. Oṃ paṃ, homage to the self consisting of marrow; from the heart [to the same place].
To the end of the left hand: *Oṃ saṃ* to the self of Śukra, salutation; from the heart to the end of the right foot.

Oṃ haṃ, salutation to the Self (ātman); [place this] from the heart to the left foot. Oṃ laṃ, salutation to the Supreme Self (paramātman); [place this] in the abdomen. Oṃ kṣaṃ, salutation to the Life-force Self (prāṇātman); [place this] in the mouth. Having thus performed the ritual placement (nyāsa), now follows the meditation (dhyāna).
Oṃ! [I bow to her] whose chest and joints are graced by arms beautifully divided by the fifty letters of the alphabet;

who wears a crescent moon bound upon her radiant crown; whose breasts are full and lofty; and who, with her lotus-like hands, clearly bears the mudrā, the rosary, the firm water-pot, and the book of knowledge.
I take refuge in the goddess of speech, who possesses three eyes and radiant splendor. Thus ends the external Mātṛkā-nyāsa.
For householders at the beginning of their stay [in that state], and for students at the beginning of creation and so forth.
And at the beginning of the withdrawal [of the ritual], one should perform the placement of the Mātṛkās for the ascetics.
Now follows the placement of the abiding (sthiti-nyāsa). The seer (ṛṣi) and the meter (chandas), however, are as before.
Meditative concentration.

I meditate upon the Goddess who possesses the luster of vermilion, whose ornaments are black, and who has three eyes; she holds a rosary of *vidyā* beads, a young deer, and an excellent arrow; and I meditate upon the golden-limbed Goddess standing at her side, holding a book and a garland of letters in her lotus-like hands. Oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ.

On the forehead: *oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*. On the face: *oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*. On the right eye: *oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*. On the left ear: *oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*. On the right nostril: *oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*. On the left nostril: *oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*.
On the nose: *oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*. On the right cheek: *oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*. On the left cheek: *oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*. On the upper lip:
*oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*. On the lower lip: *oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*. On the upper [lip]: *oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*.
In the row of teeth.
Oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ to the row of lower teeth. Oṃ ṭaṃ ṃ namaḥ to the head.

Oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ on the face. Oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ on the tip of the tongue. Oṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ at the region of the throat. Oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ at the base of the right arm. Oṃ ṭaṃ ṃ namaḥ at the right elbow. Oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ at the right wrist.

Bind: *Oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ* at the base of the right hand finger. *Oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ṇaṃ namaḥ* at the tip of the right hand finger. *Oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ* at the base of the left arm. *Oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ* at the left elbow. *Oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ* at the left [forearm].
At the wrist-joint: *oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ* on the tips of the fingers of the left hand. *Oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ* at the base of the right foot. *Oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ* on the right knee.
*Oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ* on the right ankle. *Oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ* on the right...
At the base of the toes of the right foot: *oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*. At the tips of the toes of the right foot:

*oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*. At the base of the left foot: *oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*. At the left knee: *oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*. At the left ankle: *oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*. At [the base of the left foot]: *oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*.

At the base of the toes of the left foot: *oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ṇaṃ namaḥ*. At the tips of the toes of the left foot: *oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*. On the right side: *oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*. On the left side: *oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*. On the back: *oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*. *Oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*.

Oṃ ṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ, salutation to the belly. Oṃ ṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ, salutation to the heart. Oṃ ṭaṃ ṃ, salutation to the right shoulder. Oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ, salutation to the crown of the head. Oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ, salutation to the left shoulder. Oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ, salutation from the heart to the end of the right hand. Oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ.
*Namaḥ* from the heart to the left hand: *oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*. From the heart to the right foot: *oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*. From the heart to the left foot: *oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*.
Oṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ, homage from the heart to the top of the head. Thus is the sequence of abiding.

[Ṭīkā: That which begins at the navel and is completed in the heart is to be known as the *sthiti-nyāsa*, which bestows both seen and unseen fruits. — From the *Mantra-tantra-prakāśa*. The *Sthiti-nyāsa*.
Aiṃ Bhaṃ, salutation to the navel. Aiṃ Vaṃ, salutation to the back. Aiṃ Phaṃ, salutation to the left side.
Aiṃ Paṃ Namaḥ on the right side. Aiṃ Namaḥ at the tip of the toes of the left foot. Aiṃ Dhaṃ Namaḥ at the base of the toes of the left foot. Aiṃ Daṃ Namaḥ at the ankle. Aiṃ Thaṃ...

*Aiṃ Taṃ*, salutation to the left knee. *Aiṃ Ṇaṃ*, salutation to the base of the left foot. *Aiṃ Ḍhaṃ*, salutation to the tips of the toes of the right foot. *Aiṃ Ḍaṃ*, salutation to the base of the toes of the right foot. *Aiṃ Ḍaṃ*, salutation to the right ankle. *Aiṃ Ṭhaṃ*, salutation to the right knee. *Aiṃ Ṭaṃ*.

Aiṃ Ñaṃ, salutation at the root of the right foot. Aiṃ Jhaṃ, salutation at the tips of the fingers of the left hand. Aiṃ Ñaṃ, salutation at the base of the fingers of the left hand. Aiṃ Ṇaṃ, salutation at the left wrist. Aiṃ Chaṃ, salutation at the left elbow. Aiṃ Caṃ, salutation at the root of the left upper arm. Aiṃ Ṅaṃ...
*Namaḥ* to the right wrist; *aiṃ khaṃ namaḥ* to the right elbow; *aiṃ ke namaḥ* to the root of the right arm; *aiṃ aḥ namaḥ* to the mouth; *aiṃ aṃ namaḥ* to the head;
*aiṃ auṃ namaḥ* to the lower row of teeth; *aiṃ oṃ namaḥ* to the upper row of teeth.

In the row: *Aiṃ Aiṃ* salutation to the lower lip; *Aiṃ Eṃ* salutation to the upper lip; *Aiṃ Ḷṃ* salutation to the left cheek; *Aiṃ Ḷṃ* salutation to the right cheek; *Aiṃ Ṛṃ* salutation to the left nostril; *Aiṃ Ṛṃ* salutation to the right nostril; *Aiṃ Ūṃ* salutation...
Aiṃ Uṃ Namaḥ to the left ear; Aiṃ Īṃ Namaḥ to the right ear; Aiṃ Iṃ Namaḥ to the left eye; Aiṃ Iṃ Namaḥ to the right eye; Aiṃ Oṃ Namaḥ to the circumference of the mouth; Aiṃ Aṃ Namaḥ to the forehead.

Aiṃ Yaṃ, salutation to the belly. Aiṃ Kṣaṃ, salutation to the self of vital breath (prāṇātman), to the mouth. Aiṃ Laṃ, salutation to the supreme self (paramātman), to the stomach. Aiṃ Haṃ, salutation to the self (ātman), from the heart to the left foot. Aiṃ Saṃ, salutation to the self of semen (śukrātman), from the heart to the right foot.

Aiṃ ṃ, obeisance to the self of marrow, from the heart to the left hand. Aiṃ śaṃ, obeisance to the self of bone, from the heart to the right foot. Aiṃ vaṃ, obeisance to the self of fat, on the left shoulder.
Aiṃ Laṃ, salutation to the self of bile (bhāsātman) at the crown of the head; Aiṃ Raṃ, salutation to the self of blood (asṛgātman) on the right shoulder;
Aiṃ Yaṃ, salutation to the self of skin (tvagātman) in the heart. Thus is the *sthiti-nyāsa*.
Now follows the sequence for the ritual placement (nyāsa) of emanation (sṛṣṭi).

In that regard, however, [the mantra] should be worshipped as accompanied by the Visarga, or encased within the Praṇava, or encased within the seeds of Māyā and Lakṣmī, or beginning with the Vāgbhava, or otherwise. [Now follows] the meditation (dhyāna).
Her body is adorned with fifty syllables; she holds a crescent moon and is as white as a night-lotus.
One should worship Gīrā, who has three eyes and holds a boon-granting gesture, the gesture of fearlessness, a book, and a rosary. || 1 ||

Therein, the sequence beginning with Vāgbhava is as follows: 1. *Aiṃ Aṃ namaḥ* on the forehead; *Aiṃ Āṃ namaḥ* on the circumference of the mouth; *Aiṃ Iṃ namaḥ* on the right eye; *Aiṃ Īṃ namaḥ* on the left eye; *Aiṃ Uṃ namaḥ* on the right ear; *Aiṃ Ūṃ namaḥ* on the left ear; *Aiṃ Ṛṃ namaḥ*...
Aiṃ Ṛṃ, salutation to the right nostril; Aiṃ Ṝṃ, salutation to the left nostril.
Aiṃ Ḷṃ namaḥ on the right cheek. Aiṃ Ḷṃ namaḥ on the left cheek. Aiṃ Eṃ namaḥ on the upper lip. Aiṃ namaḥ on the lower lip. Aiṃ Oṃ namaḥ.

Aiṃ Auṃ Namaḥ to the upper row of teeth. Aiṃ Aṃ Namaḥ to the lower row of teeth. Aiṃ Aḥ Namaḥ to the head. Aiṃ Kaṃ Namaḥ to the root of the left ear. Aiṃ Khaṃ Namaḥ to the left elbow. Aiṃ Gaṃ Namaḥ to the left wrist. Aiṃ Ghaṃ Namaḥ to the left... [forearm].
Aiṃ Ṅaṃ Namaḥ to the base of the fingers of the right hand. Aiṃ Caṃ Namaḥ to the tips of the fingers of the right hand.
Aiṃ Chaṃ Namaḥ to the base of the left arm. Aiṃ Jaṃ Namaḥ to the left elbow. Aiṃ Jhaṃ Namaḥ to the left wrist. Aiṃ Ñaṃ Namaḥ to the base of the fingers of the left hand.

Aiṃ Ṭaṃ Namaḥ on the tip of the left hand finger; Aiṃ Ṭhaṃ Namaḥ at the base of the right foot; Aiṃ Ṅaṃ Namaḥ on the right knee; Aiṃ Ḍhaṃ Namaḥ on the right ankle; Aiṃ Ṇaṃ Namaḥ at the base of the toes of the right foot; Aiṃ Taṃ Namaḥ on the tip of the toes of the right foot; Aiṃ [Taṃ Namaḥ] on the left...

Aiṃ Thaṃ at the base of the left foot; Aiṃ Daṃ Namaḥ at the left knee; Aiṃ Dhaṃ Namaḥ at the root of the left ankle; Aiṃ Naṃ at the tips of the toes of the left foot; Aiṃ Paṃ Namaḥ on the right side; Aiṃ Phaṃ Namaḥ on the left side; Aiṃ Vaṃ Namaḥ on the back.

Aiṃ Bhaṃ, salutation to the navel; Aiṃ Maṃ, salutation to the abdomen. Aiṃ Yaṃ, salutation to the self of skin; [salutation] to the heart. Aiṃ Raṃ, salutation to the self of blood; to the right shoulder. Aiṃ Laṃ, salutation to the self of flesh; to the crown of the head. Aiṃ Vaṃ, salutation to the self of fat; to the left shoulder.
[In the *Mantratantraprakāśa*—Ṭīkā]:
"The withdrawal (*saṃhṛti*) removes defects, and the emanation (*sṛṣṭi*) bestows sons and grandsons."
Stability is the placement of peace; therefore, it should be performed in three ways.
The placement of the planets in their respective positions is declared to bestow all accomplishments.
The renunciation of those in the first stage of life is declared to be its origin.
And the destruction of the ascetics and those dwelling in the forest has been fully described.
Even for a householder who has become dispassionate, the practice of withdrawal is ordained.
The rule for the placement of those dwelling in the forest, together with their wives, is now prescribed.
For the seeker of knowledge, even their creation is distinguished.
113) *Aiṃ śaṃ*, salutation to the self of the bones, from the heart to the right arm. *Aiṃ ṣaṃ*.

*Aiṃ Saṃ*, salutation to the *śukrātman* (semen-self), from the heart to the left arm. *Aiṃ Haṃ*, salutation to the *ātman* (self), from the heart to the left foot. *Aiṃ Laṃ*, salutation to the *paramātman* (supreme self), from the heart to the top of the head. Thus.
The ritual placement (nyāsa) according to the sequence of emanation (sṛṣṭikrama).
Now follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) according to the sequence of withdrawal (saṃhāra).
Meditative concentration.
She holds a rosary of beads, a young deer, a lofty axe, and a book in her hands; she is three-eyed and ever devoted to the Sun.
We praise the Mistress of Colors, who bears the crescent moon as her head-ornament, whose abode is the lotus,
and who is weighed down by the burden of her breasts.
One should install the Mātṛkā in reverse order in the previously mentioned locations.

Oṃ kṣaṃ namaḥ on the forehead. Oṃ haṃ namaḥ on the circumference of the face. Oṃ saṃ namaḥ on the right eye. Oṃ ṣaṃ namaḥ on the left eye. Oṃ śaṃ namaḥ on the right ear. Oṃ vaṃ namaḥ on the left ear. Oṃ laṃ namaḥ on the right nostril. Oṃ raṃ namaḥ...
*Oṃ yaṃ namaḥ* on the left nostril; *oṃ maṃ namaḥ* on the right cheek;
*oṃ bhaṃ namaḥ* on the upper lip; *oṃ baṃ namaḥ* on the lower lip; *oṃ phaṃ namaḥ* on the upper row of teeth; *oṃ paṃ namaḥ* on the lower row of teeth; *oṃ naṃ*.

*Namaḥ* on the crown of the head. *Oṃ dhaṃ namaḥ* on the perimeter of the face. *Oṃ daṃ namaḥ* at the base of the right arm. *Oṃ thaṃ namaḥ* at the right elbow. *Oṃ taṃ namaḥ* at the right wrist. *Oṃ ṇaṃ namaḥ* at the base of the fingers of the right hand. *Ḍhaṃ namaḥ* on the right...

On the tips of the fingers of the left hand: *oṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*. On the root of the left upper arm: *oṃ ṭhaṃ namaḥ*. On the left elbow: *oṃ ṭaṃ namaḥ*. On the left wrist: *oṃ ñaṃ namaḥ*. On the roots of the fingers of the left hand: *oṃ jhaṃ namaḥ*. On the tips of the fingers of the left hand: *oṃ caṃ namaḥ*.

At the base of the right foot: Oṃ Chaṃ, salutation. At the right knee: Oṃ Caṃ, salutation. At the right ankle: Oṃ Ḍaṃ, salutation. At the base of the toes of the right foot: Oṃ Ghaṃ, salutation. At the tips of the toes of the right foot: Oṃ Ghaṃ, salutation.

[According to the *Vīracūḍāmaṇitantra*: for one desiring supernatural knowledge (*vidyā*), [the mantra begins with] the Yoni-bīja and so forth; for one desiring prosperity (*śrī*), [it begins with] the syllable *Aram* and so forth; for subjugation (*vaśya*), [it begins with] the syllable *Kāma* and so forth; for paralyzing (*stambhana*), [it begins with] the syllable *Sthira-māyā* and so forth.

Oṃ Gaṃ, salutation to the root of the left foot. Oṃ Khaṃ, salutation to the left knee. Oṃ Kaṃ, salutation to the left ankle. Oṃ Aḥ, salutation to the base of the toes of the left foot. Oṃ Aṃ, salutation to the tips of the toes of the left foot. Oṃ Auṃ, salutation to the right side. Oṃ Oṃ, salutation to...

On the left side: *oṃ aiṃ namaḥ*. On the back: *oṃ eṃ namaḥ*. At the navel: *oṃ ḹṃ namaḥ*. In the belly: *oṃ ḷṃ namaḥ*. In the heart: *oṃ ḷ tvagātmane namaḥ*. On the right arm: *oṃ ṛṃ asṛgātmane namaḥ*. On the crown of the head: *oṃ ṛṃ māṃsātmane namaḥ*. [In the chest]: *oṃ ūṃ medātmane*.
*Namaḥ* on the left shoulder. *Oṃ uṃ*, salutation to the self of bone, from the heart to the right hand.

Oṃ īṃ, salutation to the self of the marrow; from the heart to the left hand. Oṃ iṃ, salutation to the self of the semen; from the heart to the right foot. Oṃ āṃ, salutation to the self; from the heart to the left foot. Oṃ aṃ, salutation to the supreme self; from the heart to the crown of the head.
Thus concludes the ritual placement (nyāsa) according to the sequence of withdrawal (saṃhāra). Now follows the ritual placement of the digits of power (śaktikalā-nyāsa).

Of this venerable Mātṛkā-nyāsa of the Śakti-kalā, Prajāpati is the seer (ṛṣi), Gāyatrī is the meter (chandaḥ), the venerable Mātṛkā Śāradā is the deity (devatā), the consonants are the seeds (bījas), and the vowels are the powers (śaktis). Its application (viniyoga) is in the Mātṛkā-nyāsa as an ancillary part of the recitation of the Saptaśatī. *Oṃ*, salutation to Prajāpati, the seer.

On the head: *Oṃ*, salutation to the Gāyatrī metre; on the face: *Oṃ*, salutation to the deity Śrī Mātṛkā Śāradā; on the heart: *Oṃ*, salutation to the consonants as seed-syllables; on the private parts: *Oṃ*, salutation to the vowels as powers; on the feet: *Oṃ*, salutation to the application (*viniyoga*); on all limbs: *Oṃ*, salutation to the application.
The ritual placement on the hands (kara-nyāsa).

Oṃ aṃ oṃ āṃ, salutation to the two thumbs (salutation to the heart). Oṃ iṃ uṃ īṃ, salutation to the two index fingers (svāhā to the head). Oṃ uṃ oṃ ūṃ, salutation to the two middle fingers (vaṣaṭ to the tuft of hair). Oṃ eṃ oṃ aiṃ...

To the two ring fingers, *namaḥ* (to the armor, *huṃ*). *Oṃ oṃ oṃ auṃ*, to the two little fingers, *namaḥ* (to the three eyes, *vauṣaṭ*). *Oṃ aṃ oṃ aḥ*, to the palms and backs of the hands, *namaḥ* (to the weapon, *phaṭ*).
(p. 115) Now, meditation (dhyāna).
Oṃ, [he holds] a conch, a discus, a lotus, an axe, a skull-cup, and a rosary.

I worship Śāradā, who possesses the luster of the moon, who holds in her hands a book, a jar of nectar, and a trident; she is endowed with five faces—white, yellow, black, white, and red—and three eyes. 1.

Oṃ hrīṃ aṃ, salutation to Nivṛtti on the forehead. Oṃ hrīṃ āṃ, salutation to Pratiṣṭhā on the face. Oṃ hrīṃ iṃ, salutation to Vidyā on the right eye. Oṃ hrīṃ īṃ, salutation to Śānti on the left eye. Oṃ hrīṃ uṃ, salutation to Indhikā on the right ear. Oṃ hrīṃ... [text truncated]

Oṃ dīpikāyai namaḥ on the left ear. Oṃ hrīṃ ṛṃ recikāyai namaḥ on the right nostril. Oṃ hrīṃ ṛṃ mocikāyai namaḥ on the left nostril. Oṃ hrīṃ ḷṃ parābhidhāyai namaḥ on the right cheek. Oṃ hrīṃ ḹṃ sūkṣmāyai namaḥ.

On the left cheek: *Oṃ hrīṃ eṃ sūkṣmāmṛtāyai namaḥ*. On the upper lip: *Oṃ hrīṃ aiṃ jñānāmṛtāyai namaḥ*. On the lower lip: *Oṃ hrīṃ oṃ āpyāyanyai namaḥ*. On the row of upper teeth: *Oṃ hrīṃ auṃ vyāpinyai namaḥ*. On the row of lower teeth: *Oṃ...*
Hrīṃ Aṃ, salutation to the one whose form is space (avyomarūpā), on the head. Oṃ Hrīṃ Aḥ, salutation to the infinite one (anantā), on the face.

Oṃ hrīṃ kaṃ, salutation to Sṛṣṭi on the tip of the tongue. Oṃ hrīṃ khaṃ, salutation to Ṛddhikā at the region of the throat. Oṃ hrīṃ gaṃ, salutation to Smṛti at the base of the right arm. Oṃ hrīṃ ghaṃ, salutation to Medhā at the right elbow. Oṃ hrīṃ ṅaṃ, salutation to Kānti...
At the right wrist: Oṃ Hrīṃ Caṃ, salutation to Lakṣmī.

At the base of the fingers of the right hand: Oṃ Hrīṃ Chaṃ, salutation to Dyuti. At the tip of the fingers of the right hand: Oṃ Hrīṃ Jaṃ, salutation to Sthirā. At the base of the left arm: Oṃ Hrīṃ Jhaṃ, salutation to Sthiti. Oṃ Hrīṃ...

Oṃ siddhyai namaḥ on the tips of the fingers of the left hand. Oṃ hrīṃ ṭaṃ jarāyai namaḥ at the base of the fingers of the left hand. Oṃ hrīṃ ṭhaṃ pālinyai namaḥ on the tips of the fingers of the left hand.

Oṃ hrīṃ ḍaṃ, obeisance to Kṣānti at the base of the right foot. Oṃ hrīṃ ḍaṃ, obeisance to Īśvarikā at the right knee. Oṃ hrīṃ ṇaṃ, obeisance to Rati at the right ankle. Oṃ hrīṃ taṃ, obeisance to Kāmikā at the base of the toes of the right foot.
Oṃ hrīṃ thaṃ, obeisance to Varadā on the tips of the toes of the right foot. Oṃ hrīṃ daṃ, obeisance to Ālhādinī at the base of the left foot. Oṃ hrīṃ dhaṃ, obeisance to Prīti.

Oṃ hrīṃ naṃ, salutation to Dīrghā at the left knee. Oṃ hrīṃ paṃ, salutation to Tīkṣṇā at the left ankle. Oṃ hrīṃ phaṃ, salutation to Raudrī at the base of the toes of the left foot. Oṃ hrīṃ baṃ, salutation to Bhayā at the right side. Oṃ...

*Hrīṃ bhaṃ*, salutation to Nidrā (Sleep) on the left side; *Oṃ hrīṃ maṃ*, salutation to Tandrīkā (Drowsiness) on the back; *Oṃ hrīṃ yaṃ*, salutation to Kṣudhā (Hunger) in the belly; *Oṃ hrīṃ raṃ*, salutation to Krodhinī (Anger) in the heart; *Oṃ hrīṃ laṃ*, salutation to Kriyā (Action) on the right shoulder; *Oṃ hrīṃ vaṃ*.
Oṃ, salutation to Utkārī on the hump. Oṃ Hrīṃ Śaṃ, salutation to Samṛtyukā on the left shoulder.

Oṃ hrīṃ ṣaṃ, obeisance to Pītā; from the heart to the right hand. Oṃ hrīṃ saṃ, obeisance to Śvetā; from the heart to the left hand. Oṃ hrīṃ haṃ, obeisance to Aruṇā; from the heart to the right foot. Oṃ hrīṃ laṃ, obeisance to Sitā; from the heart... [to the left foot].
To the end of the left foot: *oṃ hrīṃ kṣaṃ anantāyai namaḥ*, from the heart to the top of the head.
Thus ends the ritual placement of the Śaktis and Kalās.
The Nyāsa of the Śiva-kalā-mātṛkā.

Oṃ. Of this mantra for the Śrī Śivakalā Mātṛkānyāsa, Dakṣiṇāmūrti is the seer (ṛṣi), Gāyatrī is the meter (chandaḥ), Ardhanārīśvara is the deity (devatā), the consonants are the seeds (bījāni), and the vowels are the powers (śaktayaḥ). Its application (viniyoga) is in recitation (japa) for the attainment of one's desired goal. Oṃ. Salutation to Dakṣiṇāmūrti, the seer; [I place it] on the head.

Oṃ, salutations to the Gāyatrī metre; [place] on the mouth. Oṃ, salutations to the deity Ardhanārīśvara; [place] on the heart. Oṃ, salutations to the consonants, the seeds; [place] on the private parts. Oṃ, salutations to the vowels, the powers; [place] on the feet. Oṃ, salutations to the application (viniyoga); [place] on all limbs. Thus ends the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the seer and other elements.
Now follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the heart and other limbs.
Oṃ hsāṃ, salutation to both thumbs (to the heart), [salutation]. Oṃ hsīṃ, salutation to both index fingers (to the head, svāhā).
Oṃ hsūṃ, homage to the two middle fingers (vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock). Oṃ hsaiṃ, homage to the two ring fingers (huṃ to the armor). Oṃ hsauṃ.

Salutation to the two little fingers (*kaniṣṭhakābhyām namaḥ*) (for the three eyes, *vauṣaṭ*). Oṃ *hsaḥ*, salutation to the palms and backs of the hands (*karatalakarapṛṣṭhābhyām namaḥ*), for the weapon (*astrāya phaṭ*). Now, the meditation (*dhyāna*):

I worship the Lord who is half-woman (Ardhanārīśvara), who holds a noose, a goad, a boon-granting gesture, and a rosary in His hands, who has the moon as His crest-jewel, possesses three eyes, and has the luster of red gold. Oṃ Hsauṃ Aṃ:
Salutation to Śrīkaṇṭheśa and Pūrṇodarī on the forehead. Oṃ Hsauṃ Āṃ: Salutation to Ananta.

Oṃ *hsauṃ* iṃ, salutation to Sūkṣmeśa and Śālmalī at the face. Oṃ *hsauṃ* īṃ, salutation to Trimūrtīśa and Lolākṣī at the right eye. Oṃ *hsauṃ* uṃ, salutation to Amareśa and Vartulākṣī at the left eye.
At the right ear: *Oṃ hsauṃ ūṃ*, salutation to Arghīśa and Ghoṣā. At the left ear: *Oṃ hsauṃ ṛṃ*, salutation to Bhārabhūteśa and Dīrghamukhī. At the right nostril: [Oṃ hsauṃ ḷṃ].

Oṃ hsauṃ ṝṃ, salutation to Tithīya and Gomukhī at the left nostril. Oṃ hsauṃ ḷṃ, salutation to Sthāṇvīśa and Dīrghajihvā on the right cheek. Oṃ hsauṃ ḹṃ, salutation to Hara and Kuṇḍodarī on the left cheek. Oṃ hsauṃ eṃ, salutation to Jhiṃṭīśa...

*Oṃ hsauṃ aiṃ*, salutation to the two with upward-pointing hair at the upper lip. *Oṃ hsauṃ aiṃ*, salutation to Bhautikeśa and Vikṛtamukhī at the lower lip. *Oṃ hsauṃ oṃ*, salutation to Sadyojāteśa and Jvālāmukhī at the upper row of teeth. *Oṃ hsauṃ auṃ*, [salutation] to Anugraheśa and Ulkāmukhī...
Salutation to the lower row of teeth. Oṃ hsauṃ aṃ, salutation to Akrūreśa and Śrīmukhī on the head. Oṃ hsauṃ aḥ, salutation to Mahāseneśa and Vidyāmukhī on the face.
Oṃ hsauṃ kaṃ, salutation to Krodhīśa and Mahākālī at the tip of the tongue.
The procedure for the placement of mudrās.
On the forehead with the middle and ring fingers; around the face in a clockwise direction.
In all cases, the sequence begins with the south.
With the index and ring fingers for the eyes, and with the thumb for the ears.
Whatever action is performed with a mudrā yields inexhaustible fruit.
Oṃ hsauṃ khaṃ, salutation to Caṇḍeśa and Sarasvatī at the region of the throat. Oṃ hsauṃ gaṃ, salutation to Pañcāntakeśa and Sarvasiddhi-Gaurī at the base of the right arm. Oṃ...

Hsauṃ Ghaṃ, obeisance to Śivottameśa and Viśveśa, Lords of the Three Worlds, and to Vidyā; [obeisance] to the right elbow. Oṃ Hsauṃ Ṅaṃ, obeisance to Ekarudreśa and Mantra-Śakti; [obeisance] to the right wrist. Oṃ Hsauṃ Caṃ, obeisance to Kūrmeśa and Ātma-Śakti; [obeisance] to the right...

At the base of the fingers of the right hand: *oṃ hsauṃ chaṃ* to Ekanetreśa and Bhūtamātṛ, *namaḥ*. At the tips of the fingers of the right hand: *oṃ hsauṃ jaṃ* to Caturānaneśa and Lambodarī, *namaḥ*.
At the base of the left arm: *oṃ hsauṃ jhaṃ* to Ajeśa and Drāviṇī, *namaḥ*. To the left...
At the elbow: Oṃ hsauṃ ñaṃ, salutation to Sarveśa and Nāgarī at the left wrist-ornament.

Oṃ hsauṃ ṭaṃ, salutation to Someśa and Khecarī at the base of the fingers of the left hand. Oṃ hsauṃ ṭhaṃ, salutation to Lāṅgalīśa and Mañjarī at the tips of the fingers of the left hand. Oṃ hsauṃ ḍaṃ, salutation to Dārakeśa and Rūpiṇī at the right knee. Oṃ hsauṃ ḍhaṃ...

Oṃ *hsauṃ* *ṇaṃ*, salutation to Umākānteśa and Kākodarī at the base of the right foot. Oṃ *hsauṃ* *taṃ*, salutation to Āṣāḍhīśa and Pūtanā at the right ankle. Oṃ *hsauṃ* *thaṃ*... [at the base of the toes of the right foot].
Salutation to Caṇḍīśa and Bhadrakālī on the tips of the toes of the right foot.

[Touch] the two nostrils with the little fingers and thumbs; the two cheeks with the middle fingers; the two lips with the middle fingers; the two rows of teeth with the ring fingers; the head with the middle fingers;
and the mouth with the ring and middle fingers.
The Exposition of Mudrās.
The etymological derivation of *mudrā* is "that which bestows joy" (*mudaṃ rāti dadāti*). Indeed, all the deities rejoice in this very [mudrā].
By this, the following is indicated: "But during worship, at the time of recitation, in meditation, and in rites performed with desire."

The respective mudrās should be employed to bring the deities into presence. In all cases hereafter, [the placement] is with the little finger; in the absence of a specific instruction, one should place [the mudrās] everywhere with the ring finger and the thumb. These are the six-limbed (ṣaḍaṅga) mudrās of Śakti according to the Āgama.
Excluding the thumb, the four fingers [are placed] at the heart and the head; at the crest (śikhā), the fist should be formed;
the thumb should be placed against the nose; and from all the fingers down to the navel, the hands form the binding of armor (kavaca). Thus it is said.
Oṃ hsauṃ daṃ, salutation to Antrīśa and Yoginī at the base of the left foot. Oṃ hsauṃ dhaṃ, salutation to Mīneśa and Śaṅkhinī at the left knee. Oṃ hsauṃ naṃ...

Oṃ hsauṃ maṃ Meṣeśa and Tarjanī, salutation to the left ankle. Oṃ hsauṃ paṃ Lohiteśa and Kālarātrī, salutation to the base of the toes of the left foot. Oṃ hsauṃ phaṃ Śikhīśa and Kubjinī, salutation to the tips of the toes of the left foot. Oṃ hsauṃ vaṃ Chagalaṇḍeśa...

Salutation to Kapardinī on the right side. Oṃ hsauṃ bhaṃ, salutation to Dviraṇḍeśa and Vajrī on the left side. Oṃ hsauṃ maṃ, salutation to Mahākāleśa and Jayā on the abdomen. Oṃ hsauṃ raṃ, [salutation] to Asṛgātman and Bhujageśa Revatī.

*Namaḥ* to the heart. *Oṃ hsauṃ laṃ*, obeisance to Pinākīśa and Mādhavī, who are of the nature of flesh, to the right shoulder. *Oṃ hsauṃ vaṃ*, obeisance to Khaḍgīśa and Vāruṇī, who are of the nature of fat, to the back of the neck (*kakudi*). *Oṃ hsauṃ śaṃ*, [obeisance] to Bakeśa and Vāyavī, who are of the nature of bone...

*Namaḥ* on the left shoulder. *Oṃ hsauṃ ṣaṃ*, salutation to Śveteśa and Vidāriṇī, who are of the nature of marrow; from the heart to the right hand. *Oṃ hsauṃ saṃ*, salutation to Bhṛgvīśa and Sahajā, who are of the nature of semen; from the heart to the left [hand].

To the end of the hands: *Oṃ hsauṃ haṃ*, salutation to Nakulīśa and Lakṣmī, the two souls of the vital breath (*prāṇātman*); from the heart to the right foot. *Oṃ hsauṃ laṃ*, salutation to Śiveśa and Vyāpinī; from the heart to the left foot. *Hsauṃ kṣaṃ*, salutation to Krodhātman and Bhayā, [and] Saṃvartakeśa.
Salutation to Mahāmāyā from the heart to the top of the head.
A devotee should likewise perform the nyāsa and other rites for Śrīkaṇṭha and the others, as stated in the twenty-first wave of the Mantramahodadhi.
Now follows the method for the sixteen-fold placement (ṣoḍhā-nyāsa) of Śakti. Therein, first is the placement of the pure Mātṛkās:
*aṃ āṃ iṃ īṃ uṃ ūṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ* at the heart;
*eṃ aiṃ oṃ auṃ aṃ aḥ kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ namaḥ* on the right arm; *ṅaṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ*.
Jhaṃ ñaṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ, obeisance to the left arm. Ṇaṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ, obeisance to the right foot.
*Maṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ laṃ kṣaṃ namo* on the left foot. Thus ends the first [rite], the placement of the pure *mātṛkā*.
Now follows the second ritual placement (nyāsa).

Śrīṃ Aṃ Śrīṃ Aṃ Śrīṃ Aṃ, salutation to the forehead. Śrīṃ Āṃ Śrīṃ Āṃ Śrīṃ Āṃ, salutation to the face. Śrīṃ Iṃ Śrīṃ Iṃ Śrīṃ Iṃ, salutation to the right eye. Śrīṃ Īṃ Śrīṃ Īṃ Śrīṃ Īṃ, salutation to the left eye. Śrīṃ Uṃ Śrīṃ Uṃ Śrīṃ Uṃ, salutation to...

*Śrīṃ ūṃ śrīṃ ūṃ śrīṃ ūṃ namaḥ* to the right ear. *Śrīṃ ṛṃ śrīṃ ṛṃ śrīṃ ṛṃ namaḥ* to the left ear. *Śrīṃ ṝṃ śrīṃ ṝṃ śrīṃ ṝṃ namaḥ* to the right nostril. *Śrīṃ ḷṃ śrīṃ ḷṃ namaḥ* to the left nostril. *Śrīṃ ḷṃ śrīṃ ḷṃ namaḥ* to the right [nostril].
On the left cheek: *śrīṃ ḷṃ śrīṃ ḷṃ śrīṃ ḷ*. Homage on the left cheek:
*śrīṃ eṃ śrāṃ eṃ śrīṃ eṃ*. Homage on the upper lip: *śrīṃ aiṃ śrī aiṃ śrīṃ aiṃ*. Homage on the lower lip: *śrīṃ oṃ śrīṃ oṃ śrīṃ oṃ*. Homage on the upper row of teeth: *śrīṃ oṃ śrīṃ oṃ śrīṃ oṃ*.

*Śrīṃ oṃ śrīṃ oṃ śrīṃ oṃ*, salutation to the row of lower teeth. *Śrīṃ aṃ śrīṃ aṃ śrīṃ aṃ*, salutation to the head. *Śrīṃ aḥ śrīṃ aḥ śrīṃ aḥ*, salutation to the mouth. *Śrīṃ kaṃ śrīṃ kaṃ śrīṃ kaṃ*, salutation to the root of the right arm. *Śrīṃ*... [and so forth].

*Khaṃ śrīṃ khaṃ śrīṃ khaṃ*, salutations to the right elbow. *Śrīṃ gaṃ śrīṃ gaṃ śrīṃ gaṃ*, salutations to the right wrist. *Śrīṃ ghaṃ śrīṃ ghaṃ śrīṃ ghaṃ*, salutations to the base of the fingers of the right hand. *Śrīṃ ṅaṃ śrīṃ ṅaṃ śrīṃ ṅaṃ*, salutations...
*Śrīṃ caṃ śrīṃ caṃ śrīṃ caṃ namaḥ* at the tip of the fingers of the right hand;
*śrīṃ chaṃ śrīṃ chaṃ śrīṃ chaṃ namaḥ* at the base of the left arm; *śrīṃ chaṃ śrīṃ chaṃ śrīṃ chaṃ namaḥ* at the left elbow.

Śrī. Jaṃ Śrīṃ Jaṃ Śrīṃ Jaṃ, salutations to the left wrist-joint. Śrīṃ Jhaṃ Śrīṃ Jhaṃ Śrīṃ Jhaṃ, salutations to the base of the fingers of the left hand. Śrīṃ Ñaṃ Śrīṃ Ñaṃ Śrīṃ Ñaṃ, salutations to the tips of the fingers of the left hand. Śrīṃ Ṭaṃ Śrīṃ Ṭaṃ Śrī Ṭaṃ.

Namo at the base of the right foot: Śrīṃ Ṭhaṃ Śrīṃ Ṭhaṃ Śrīṃ Ṭhaṃ. Namo at the right knee: Śrīṃ Ḍaṃ Śrīṃ Ḍaṃ Śrīṃ Ḍaṃ. Namo at the right ankle: Śrīṃ Ḍhaṃ Śrīṃ Ḍhaṃ Śrīṃ Ḍhaṃ. Namo at the base of the toes of the right foot: Śrīṃ Ṇaṃ Śrīṃ...
Ṇaṃ Śrīṃ Ṇaṃ; salutation to the tip of the big toe of the right foot.
*Śrīṃ taṃ śrīṃ taṃ śrīṃ taṃ*, salutation at the base of the left foot. *Śrīṃ thaṃ śrīṃ thaṃ śrīṃ thaṃ*, salutation at the left knee. *Śrīṃ daṃ śrīṃ daṃ śrīṃ daṃ*, salutation... [at the left thigh].

At the left ankle: *Śrīṃ dhaṃ śrīṃ dhaṃ śrīṃ dhaṃ namaḥ*. At the base of the toes of the left foot: *Śrīṃ naṃ śrīṃ naṃ śrī naṃ namaḥ*. At the tips of the toes of the left foot: *Śrīṃ paṃ śrīṃ paṃ śrīṃ paṃ namaḥ*. On the right side: *Śrīṃ phaṃ śrīṃ*.

*Phaṃ śrīṃ phaṃ*, salutation on the left side. *Śrīṃ baṃ śrīṃ baṃ śrīṃ baṃ*, salutation on the back. *Śrīṃ bhaṃ śrīṃ bhaṃ śrīṃ bhaṃ*, salutation at the navel. *Śrī maṃ śrīṃ maṃ śrīṃ maṃ*, salutation in the heart. *Śrīṃ yaṃ śrīṃ yaṃ śrīṃ yaṃ*.
*Oṃ* *tvagātmane namaḥ* in the heart; *śrīṃ raṃ śrīṃ raṃ śrīṃ raṃ asṛgātmane namaḥ* on the right shoulder; *śrīṃ laṃ śrīṃ laṃ śrīṃ laṃ māṃsātmane namaḥ* at the back of the neck;
*śrīṃ vaṃ śrīṃ vaṃ śrīṃ vaṃ medātmane namaḥ* on the left shoulder.

*Śrīṃ śaṃ śrīṃ śaṃ śrīṃ śaṃ*, salutation to the self of bone (*asthyātman*), from the heart to the right hand. *Śrīṃ ṣaṃ śrīṃ ṣaṃ śrīṃ ṣaṃ*, salutation to the self of marrow (*majjātman*), from the heart to the left hand. *Śrīṃ saṃ śrīṃ saṃ śrīṃ saṃ*, salutation to the self of semen (*śukrātman*).

From *dayā* to the end of the right foot: *śrīṃ haṃ śrīṃ haṃ śrīṃ haṃ ātmane namaḥ*, from the heart to the end of the left foot. In the abdomen: *śrīṃ laṃ śrīṃ laṃ śrīṃ laṃ paramātmane namaḥ*. *śrīṃ kṣaṃ śrīṃ kṣaṃ śrīṃ kṣaṃ prāṇātmane namaḥ*.
From the heart to the top of the head. Thus is the second placement (nyāsa).
Now follows the third ritual placement (nyāsa).

*klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ*—*namaḥ* to the forehead. *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ*—*namaḥ* to the face. *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ*—*namaḥ* to the right eye. *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ*—*namaḥ* to the left eye. *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ*... [and so forth].
Śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ, salutation to the right ear. Klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ, salutation to the left ear. Klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ, salutation to the right nostril.
*klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ*, salutation to the left nostril; *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ*, salutation to the right cheek; *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ*, salutation to the left cheek.
p.
122) *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ* obeisance to the upper lip; *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ* obeisance to the lower lip;
*klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ* obeisance...

*klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ* to the upper row of teeth. *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ* to the lower row of teeth. *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ* to the head. *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ* to the mouth. *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ* to...
At the base of the right arm: *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*. At the right elbow: *dakṣa-kūrpare*.
*klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ*, salutations to the right wrist;

*klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ*, salutations to the base of the fingers of the right hand; *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ*, salutations to the tips of the fingers of the right hand; *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ*.

Namo vāma-bāhu-mūle | Klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namo vāma-kūrpare | Klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namo vāma-maṇibandhe | Klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namo vāma-hastāṅguli-mūle | Klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ...

*Śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ*, salutations to the tips of the fingers of the left hand. *Klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ*, salutations to the root of the right foot. *Klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ*, salutations to the right knee. *Klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ*, salutations to the right ankle. *Klīṃ*... [and so forth].

*Śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ*, salutations to the base of the right toe. *Klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ*, salutations to the tip of the right toe. *Klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ*, salutations to the base of the left foot. *Klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ*, salutations to the left...
At the knee: *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ* at the base of the toes of the left foot.

*klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ*, salutation at the tips of the toes of the left foot; *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ*, salutation on the right side; *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ*, salutation on the left side; *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ*, salutation...
On the back: *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*. At the navel: *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*.
On the abdomen: *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*.

p. 123) *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ* homage to the self of the skin, in the heart; *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ* homage to the self of blood, on the right shoulder; *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ*... [and so forth].

*Śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ*, obeisance to the self of flesh at the hump of the neck (*kakudi*). *Klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ*, obeisance to the self of marrow in the left shoulder (*vāmāṃse*). *Klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ*, obeisance to the self of bone from the heart up to the right hand (*hṛdayādi dakṣahastāntam*). *Klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ*.

*klīṃ śrīṃ* salutation to the self of marrow, from the heart to the left hand; *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ* salutation to the self of semen, from the heart to the right foot; *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ* salutation to the supreme self (*paramātman*) in the abdomen; *klīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ*.
Śrīṃ Klīṃ Śrīṃ [from] the heart to the top of the head. This is the third nyāsa.
Now follows the fourth nyāsa.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Namaḥ on the forehead.
The fifth.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ Cāmuṇḍāyai Vicce Hrāṃ Hrāṃ Ṛṃ Ṛṃ Klūṃ Namaḥ on the forehead.
The sixth is the direct order.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ Cāmuṇḍāyai Vicce Namaḥ on the forehead.
The reverse placement (viloma-nyāsa).
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ Cāmuṇḍāyai Vicce Namaḥ, from the heart to the top of the head.
The deposition of the principles (tattvanyāsa).
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ, salutation to the principle of the self (ātmatattva), from the feet up to the navel.
*Śivatattvāya namaḥ* from the heart to the head. *Vicce śivatattvāya namaḥ* from the heart to the head.
The placement of syllables (akṣaranyāsa).

Aiṃ, salutation to the aperture of Brahmā (the crown of the head). Hrīṃ, salutation between the eyebrows. Klīṃ, salutation to the forehead. Cāṃ, salutation to the heart. Muṃ, salutation to the two sides of the belly. Ḍāṃ, salutation to the navel.
Yaiṃ, salutation to the *liṅga*; viṃ, salutation to the secret place; cceṃ, salutation to the face. Thus.
Hrīṃ klīṃ, [salutation] to Cāmuṇḍā, Vicce!

Then, while reciting the root mantra nine times, seven times, or five times, one should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-nyāsa*) with both hands crossed. Thereafter, having constructed the yantra according to the prescribed method— consisting of a point, a triangle, a hexagon, an eight-petaled lotus, a twenty-four-petaled lotus, and a square enclosure— and having placed it upon the pedestal;

One should perform the ritual placement of the seats (*pīṭhanyāsa*). Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the Support-Energy (*ādhāra-śakti*). Oṃ, obeisance to Primordial Nature (*prakṛti*). Oṃ, obeisance to the Tortoise (*kūrma*). Oṃ, obeisance to the Ocean of Nectar (*sudhāmbudhi*). Oṃ, obeisance to the Isle of Jewels (*maṇidvīpa*). Oṃ, obeisance to the House of the Wish-Fulfilling Gem (*cintāmaṇigṛha*). Oṃ, obeisance to the Cremation Ground (*śmaśāna*). Oṃ...

Salutation to the Pārijāta tree. At its root: Oṃ, salutation to the jeweled altar (ratnavedikā); Oṃ, salutation to the gem-studded pedestal (maṇipīṭha). One should place these two in the heart. In the four directions: Oṃ, salutation to the various sages; Oṃ, salutation to the various gods; Oṃ, salutation to the corpses; Oṃ, salutation to the skulls of the corpses.
Salutation to the corpses from which much flesh, bone, and marrow are being consumed. Oṃ, salutation to Dharma on the right shoulder;

Oṃ, salutation to Jñāna on the left shoulder; Oṃ, salutation to Vairāgya on the left thigh; Oṃ, salutation to Aiśvarya on the right thigh; Oṃ, salutation to Adharma on the face; Oṃ, salutation to Ajñāna...

Homage to the left side. Oṃ, homage to Avairājñā (the lack of sovereignty) at the navel. Oṃ, homage to Anaiśvaryā (lack of power) on the right side. Then, in the heart: Oṃ, homage to Ānandakanda (the bulb of bliss). Oṃ, homage to Saṃvinnāla (the stalk of consciousness). Oṃ, homage to the lotus consisting of all principles (tattvas). Oṃ, homage to Prakṛti...
Oṃ, salutation to the petals consisting of *māyā*. Oṃ, salutation to the filaments consisting of transformations (*vikāra*).
Oṃ, salutation to the pericarp enriched with the fifty seed-syllables (*bīja*). Oṃ, aṃ, salutation to the solar orb (*sūryamaṇḍala*) whose essence consists of the twelve *kalās*.
Oṃ saṃ, obeisance to the lunar maṇḍala, whose essence consists of sixteen digits. Oṃ maṃ, obeisance to the fire maṇḍala, whose essence consists of ten digits. Oṃ saṃ, obeisance to sattva. Oṃ raṃ.

Oṃ, salutation to Rajas. Oṃ Taṃ, salutation to Tamas. Oṃ Āṃ, salutation to the Self (Ātman). Oṃ Aṃ, salutation to the Inner Self (Antarātman). Oṃ Paṃ, salutation to the Supreme Self (Paramātman). Oṃ Hrīṃ, salutation to the Self of Knowledge (Jñānātman). In the eight directions: Oṃ Iṃ, salutation to Will (Ichchā). Oṃ Jñāṃ, salutation to Knowledge (Jñānā).

Oṃ kriṃ, salutation to Kriyā. Oṃ kāṃ, salutation to Kāminī. Oṃ kāṃ, salutation to Kāmadāyinī. Oṃ raṃ, salutation to Rati. Oṃ raṃ, salutation to Ratipriyā. Oṃ āṃ, salutation to Ānandā, in the center. Oṃ maṃ, salutation to Manonmanī. Oṃ paṃ, salutation to Parā.

Salutation! Oṃ Paṃ, salutation to Parāparā. Oṃ Hsauḥ, salutation to the lotus-seat of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, and the Great Preta. Having thus performed the placement of the seat (pīṭha-nyāsa), one should meditate upon Durgā there.
Oṃ! [I bow to her] who holds a conch, a discus, a mace, arrows, a bow, an iron club, a trident, a *bhuśuṇḍī* weapon, a sword, and a bell, and who possesses ten faces.
I bow to Mahākālī, who is dark-hued and characterized by the quality of tamas, who has ten feet, and who holds a garland,
an axe, arrows, a mace, and a thunderbolt.
A lotus, a bow, a water-pot, a staff, a spear, a sword,
as well as a shield, a lily, a bell, a vessel for liquor, and a trident.
I worship Mahālakṣmī, the crusher of Mahiṣa, who stands upon a lotus, possesses a reddish luster, and holds a noose and the Sudarśana discus. || 4 ||
I bow to the radiant Goddess born from Gaurī, who holds a bell, a trident, a plow, a conch, a mace, an enemy-slaying bow, and arrows.
Having meditated thus and worshipped with mental offerings, one should prostrate.

[Note—The five vessels for *arghya*, *pādya*, *ācamanīya*, *madhuparka*, and *ācamana* should be placed to one's own right, along with flowers and other offerings; see *Mantramahodadhi*, Chapter 21, Verse 75.
The Procedure for Establishing the Special *Arghya* Vessel.
Having drawn a bindu, a triangle, and a square between oneself and the Śrīcakra (1),
one should stabilize [the deity] with the conch-gesture (śaṅkhamudrā) in the center (2).
(126) Having worshipped the bell with "Oṃ jayadhvani mātaḥ svāhā," one should ring it, [reciting]: "Oṃ,
for the purpose of the arrival of the gods and for the departure of the demons, [I ring] the sound of the bell."
One should perform that which causes delight to the deity.
Having written the nine-syllable mantra in the center and sprinkled it with the water of the general *arghya*, then [worship] in the corners of the square:
*oṃ pūrṇagiri-pīṭhāya namaḥ* in the east; *oṃ uḍḍīyāna-pīṭhāya namaḥ* in the south;
*oṃ kāmarūpa-pīṭhāya namaḥ* in the west; *oṃ jālandhara-* [in the north].

"Salutation to the Pīṭha in the north. Having worshipped the triangle with the three parts of the root mantra, and having worshipped it with "Oṃ Hrīṃ, salutation to Ādhāraśakti," one should worship the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga) within the six corners.

There, having placed the *arghya* vessel upon the base and sprinkled it with the water of the general *arghya* while reciting "Namaḥ," [one should offer worship] with: "Maṃ, obeisance to the fire-maṇḍala consisting of ten digits.
"Oṃ Yaṃ, obeisance to Dhūmrārcis. "Oṃ Raṃ, obeisance to Ūṣmā. "Oṃ Laṃ..."
Salutation to Jvālinī. Oṃ vaṃ, salutation to Jvālinī. Oṃ śaṃ, salutation to Visphuliṅginī.
Oṃ ṣaṃ, obeisance to Suśrī. Saṃ, obeisance to Svarūpā. Oṃ haṃ, obeisance to Kapilā.
Having worshipped with "Oṃ laṃ, obeisance to Havyavāhā," and having washed the vessel with "Oṃ phaṭ."
"Oṃ, I establish the special *arghya* vessel for Śrī Durgā; obeisance. Having thus established the vessel:
"Oṃ aṃ, obeisance to the solar disc (*arka-maṇḍala*), the *arghya* vessel consisting of twelve kalās. Oṃ kaṃ bhaṃ, obeisance to Tapinī. Oṃ khaṃ baṃ, obeisance to Tāpinī. Oṃ gaṃ phaṃ..."
Salutation to Dhūmrā. Oṃ Ghaṃ Paṃ, salutation to Marīcī. Oṃ Ṅa Naṃ, salutation to Jvālinī. Oṃ Caṃ Dhaṃ, salutation to Ruci. Oṃ Chaṃ Daṃ, salutation to Suṣumṇā.

Oṃ jaṃ khaṃ, salutation to Bhogadā. Oṃ jhaṃ taṃ, salutation to Viśvā. Oṃ ñaṃ ṇaṃ, salutation to Bodhinī. Oṃ ṭaṃ ḍhaṃ, salutation to Dhāriṇī. Oṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ, salutation to Kṣamā. Having thus worshipped, one should recite the Mātṛkā in reverse order while chanting the root mantra.
Having filled the jar with water (or water from a sacred ford), saying, "I fill the arghya vessel."
There, having placed red sandalwood, flowers, and so forth;
Oṃ saṃ, obeisance to the lunar maṇḍala, whose essence consists of sixteen digits. Oṃ aṃ, obeisance to Amṛtā. Oṃ āṃ, obeisance to Mānadā. Oṃ iṃ, obeisance to Pūṣā. Oṃ īṃ, obeisance to Tuṣṭi.

Salutation! Oṃ uṃ, salutation to Puṣṭi (Nourishment). Oṃ ūṃ, salutation to Rati (Delight). Oṃ ṛṃ, salutation to Dhṛti (Fortitude). Oṃ ṝṃ, salutation to Śaśinī (the Moon-like One). Oṃ ḷṃ, salutation to Caṇḍikā (the Fierce One). Oṃ ḹṃ, salutation to Kānti (Beauty). Oṃ eṃ, salutation to Jyotsnā (Moonlight). Oṃ aiṃ, salutation to Śrī (Prosperity). Oṃ oṃ.

Salutation to Prīti. Oṃ Auṃ, salutation to Aṅgadā. Oṃ Aṃ, salutation to Pūrṇā. Oṃ Aḥ, salutation to Pūrṇāmṛtā. Having thus worshipped, one should draw a triangle, a circle, and a hexagon with *kuśa* grass;
then, within that, upon the line of the triangle, [place] aṃ, āṃ, iṃ, īṃ, uṃ, ūṃ, ṛṃ, ṝṃ.

Having written the syllables *ḷṃ*, *ḹṃ*, *eṃ*, *aiṃ*, *oṃ*, *auṃ*, *aṃ*, *aḥ*, *kaṃ*, *khaṃ*, *gaṃ*, *ghaṃ*, *ṅaṃ*, *caṃ*, *chaṃ*, *jaṃ*, *jhaṃ*, *ñaṃ*, *ṭaṃ*, *ṭhaṃ*, *ḍaṃ*, *ḍhaṃ*, *ṇaṃ*, *taṃ*, *thaṃ*, *daṃ*, *dhaṃ*, *naṃ*, *paṃ*,
*phaṃ*, *baṃ*, *bhaṃ*, *maṃ*, *yaṃ*, *raṃ*, *laṃ*, *vaṃ*, *śaṃ*, *ṣaṃ*, *saṃ* within a triangle, thus it is written.

Having written "haṃ laṃ kṣaṃ" in the center of the line and worshipped the triangle with the three root-mantra sections, and having worshipped the six limbs (aṅgas) in the six corners, [one should recite]: "O Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Godāvarī, Sarasvatī, Kāverī, Narmadā, and Sindhu, be present in this water! Oṃ."

"O Sun, by the truth that the holy waters of the interior of the cosmic egg have been touched by your rays— by that truth, O Lord, O Maker of Day, grant me the sacred water (tīrtha)! With this mantra, having invoked the holy waters from the solar orb using the *aṅkuśa-mudrā*, [one offers] a flower with "vauṣaṭ" and performs the *gālinī-mudrā* with "vaṣaṭ."
[Note 1: As for the *gālanī* mudrā—The little fingers and thumbs of the two hands are joined together with one another; the index, middle, and ring fingers are unjoined, bent, and turned away.
Having displayed the mudrā:

In the *Dharmasāra*: "Having offered water for the feet (*pādya*), the respectful offering (*arghya*), and water for sipping (*ācamanīya*) into the conch and the jar, and having consecrated oneself as well as all the ritual materials for worship with [that water], one should perform the worship."

In the *Pūjāsāgara*: One should worship a water-pot filled with well-perfumed water on the left, using the mantra beginning with "kalaśasya"; thereafter, one should invoke the sacred waters (*tīrthas*).
In the left [hands], he holds a water-vessel, an umbrella, a mirror, and a fly-whisk;
with palms joined in reverence, he should bow to his gurus and Gaṇapati with his left and right [hands].
1. The Characteristics of the Conch Mudrā: Having grasped the left thumb with the right fist, one should turn the fist upward and then extend the thumb.
The fingers of the left hand thus joined together and well extended,
with the thumb of the right hand touching them, is the conch mudrā, which bestows prosperity.
p.
128) Salutation to the Goddess Durgā, whose nature consists of the three qualities (triguṇa). Having thus meditated upon her and performed worship, [one should proceed].

One should worship the jewels in the sequence starting from the east with their respective mantras: Oṃ glūṃ, obeisance to the jewels of the sky (gagana-ratna). Oṃ slūṃ, obeisance to the jewels of heaven (svarga-ratna). Oṃ mlūṃ, obeisance to the jewels of the mortal world (martya-ratna). Oṃ nlūṃ, obeisance to the jewels of the netherworld (nāga-ratna). Oṃ plūṃ, [obeisance to the jewels] of the subterranean realm (pātāla).
"Salutation to the Jewels. Having thus worshipped, one should then meditate upon Ānandabhairava and Ānandabhairavī.
Resembling ten million suns and as cool as ten million moons,
the god has eighteen arms, five faces, and three eyes.
Seated upon a lotus in the midst of the ocean of nectar, he is Brahmā,
mounted upon a bull, blue-throated, and adorned with all ornaments.
The god holds a skull-cup and a khaṭvāṅga staff, sounds a bell and a ḍamaru drum,
and bears a noose, a goad, a mace, and a club.
A sword, a shield, a spear, a mallet, a trident, and a staff;
a variegated shield, a severed head, and hands displaying the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness.

The most excellent practitioner should meditate upon the Lord of Gods, Lohita. Having rendered [the water] nectar by means of the *vaṃ* syllable and the *dhenu* mudrā twice, he should sprinkle himself and the materials for worship with that water. Thus is the procedure for the special *arghya*.

Now, the ritual for piercing the site (kṣetra-kīlana). Having gone to the place of recitation (japa-sthāna), one should perform the formal acquisition of the earth. As follows: "For the sake of accomplishing the preparatory rite (puraścaraṇa) of this mantra which has been taken up, I take hold of this earth so that this mantra may attain success. Having thus grasped the earth:

Ten stakes, each one *vitasti* in length, made from any one of the *aśvattha*, *udumbara*, or *plakṣa* trees; these have been consecrated one hundred and eight times with the mantra: "Oṃ, obeisance to the Sudarśana weapon, Phaṭ! [The mantra continues:
"Oṃ, and those who are creators of obstacles here, whether dwelling on earth, in heaven, or in the intermediate space, and those who are obstructive spirits..."
And others [are successful] in the accomplishments of my mantra. || 1 ||
May they all depart from afar, leaving this field secured by this ritual stake; may there be success for me without obstacles. || 2 ||
With these two mantras, one should drive ten stakes into the ten directions. Then, having worshipped each stake individually with the mantra: *oṃ namaḥ sudarśanāya astrāya phaṭ*.
Having offered an oblation of black gram and cooked rice to the guardians of the directions, the guardians of the field, and Gaṇapati.
Having performed the external purification (*ācamana*) and breath control (*prāṇāyāma*), [reciting] "Today here... and so forth,

for the attainment of the fruits mentioned in the ritual manual (*kalpa*) for myself, the sacrificer (*yajamāna*), and for the successful completion of the *puraścaraṇa* of the goddess Śrī Durgā, [I offer] five [oblations] to the deities beginning with Vaṭuka in the four directions, using substances of curd and black-gram rice.
I shall perform the offering of the great elements (mahābhūta-bali).

On the eastern part of the ground, having drawn with vermilion (sindūra) a yantra consisting of a dot, a triangle, a circle, and a square; having worshipped it with scents and flowers, saying: "Obeisance to the mandala which is the support for the vessel of Vaṭuka’s offering";
and having placed the support and the offering of food along with various side dishes; [one recites]: "Oṃ Vaṃ, O Vaṭuka..."

Having worshipped with scents and flowers, saying "Salutation to the sacrificial offering (balidravya)," and having worshipped in the east, saying "Vaṃ, salutation to Vaṭuka," and having presented the oblation: Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, come, come, O son of the Goddess, Lord Vaṭuka, tawny one, radiant with a mass of matted hair, three-eyed, flame-mouthed; destroy, destroy all obstacles!
"Accept the bali offering together with all ritual services, svāhā. With this, one should release the bali with the left thumb and ring finger, and discard water with the right hand.
A Prayer.
Oṃ! He holds a skull-cup in his hand, wears earrings, carries a staff in his grasp, and has a young, dark-blue serpent as his sacred thread.

Victorious is Vaṭukanātha, the bestower of success upon practitioners, whose worship at the time of the ritual is the cause for the removal of obstacles! May Vaṭuka, satisfied by the offering of the *bali*, who grants all accomplishments and is attended by spirits (*bhūtas*) and *vetālas*, constantly grant me peace. Thus, one should offer a handful of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*).

Having drawn the entrails (antra) on the right of the wheel as before, one should worship with scents and flowers, saying: "Obeisance to the maṇḍala which is the support for the sacrificial vessel (balipātra) of the Yoginīs. Then, having placed upon it the support and the sacrificial offering (bali) together with food and side-dishes, one should [worship] with scents and flowers, saying: "Oṃ yāṃ, obeisance to the substance for the Yoginī-bali."

Having worshipped [her], and having worshipped on the right with "Oṃ, obeisance to all the Yoginīs," and having presented the *bali* offering, one should cast forth the *bali* with the left thumb, middle finger, and ring finger, reciting: "Oṃ, to the Yoginīs of all castes, accept this *bali*, twice, hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. One should discard water with the right hand.
Prayer.
Oṃ! Whether above the Brahmāṇḍa, or in heaven, in the expanse of the sky, on the surface of the earth, or in the partless realm;
Whether in the netherworld, on land, in fire, in water, in wind, or wherever else they may be situated;

May those who have established their presence in the fields, seats, and secondary seats in every direction, who are ever pleased by offerings of incense, lamps, and the like, and who are worshipped by the lords of heroes— may they, possessing the power to perform auspicious rites, protect us forever.
May whatever Yoginīs there are—whether fierce, gentle, terrible, or beyond the supreme; whether moving in the sky, moving on the earth, or pervading space—be forever pleased with me.
To the Yoginīs, svāhā! To all the Yoginīs, phaṭ! One should offer a handful of flowers.

Having drawn the yantra on the western side of the wheel as before, one should worship it with scents and flowers, saying: "Obeisance to the mandala which is the support for the vessel of the bali offering to the Kṣetrapāla."

Having placed the base offering (*ādhāra*) and the sacrificial oblation (*bali*) accompanied by food and condiments, one should worship with scents and flowers, saying: "Oṃ kṣaṃ, salutation to the Kṣetrapāla and the materials for the oblation. Then, having worshipped in the west, saying: "kṣaṃ, salutation to Kṣetrapāla," and having presented the oblation, [one recites]: "kṣāṃ kṣīṃ kṣūṃ kṣaiṃ kṣauṃ kṣaḥ. O, Stāna..."

"O Guardian of the Field (Kṣetrapāla), accept this offering (bali)! Fulfill all desires! Svāhā! One should cast forth the offering with the left thumb and forefinger, and discard water with the right hand.
A Prayer.
And the field-protector who dwells in that field, together with his attendants.
"May he, pleased by this offering of bali, grant me protection from all [harm]. One should offer a handful of flowers.

To the north of the wheel, having drawn the yantra as before, one should worship it with scents and flowers, saying: "Oṃ Gaṃ, obeisance to the mandala which is the support for the vessel of the offering to Gaṇeśa. Then, worshipping the substance with scents and flowers, saying: "Obeisance to the substance," and then worshipping Gaṇeśa to the north, saying: "Oṃ Gaṃ, obeisance to Gaṇeśa," one should present the offering.

*gāṃ gīṃ gūṃ gaiṃ gauṃ gaḥ gaṇapataye varavarada sarvajanaṃ me vaśamānaya sarvopacārasahitaṃ baliṃ gṛhṇa 2 svāhā* || With this, one should offer the *bali* with the left thumb and middle finger, and discard the water with the right hand.
A Prayer.
May all my undertakings at all times be accomplished without obstacle.
May the Lord of Obstacles, together with his Śakti, grant constant peace. [One should offer a handful of flowers.]

Having drawn a four-cornered yantra on one's left, and having worshipped it with scents and flowers while reciting "Hrīṃ, obeisance to the mandala that is the support for the vessel of the bali-offering made by all obstructing spirits," one should place upon it the supporting vessel containing the bali-offering consisting of rice and side-dishes,
[reciting] "To the substance of the bali-offering made by all obstructing spirits."
*Namaḥ*. Having thus worshipped with perfume and flowers, and having presented the *bali* offering: *Oṃ hrīṃ, to all you who create obstacles, to all beings, accept this bali, twice! Huṃ phaṭ svāhā!*
Thus, one should offer the bali-oblation with all the fingers; one should discard the water with the right hand.
Prayer.
Those beings who are creators of obstacles, whether they dwell in heaven, on earth, or in the intermediate space;
And those residing in the regions of Pātāla were purified by the yoga of Śiva.
The hundred-fold [groups] beginning with the Krūras, as well as those beginning with the Pākhaṇḍas, are established.
Dhruva and others, whose friendship is truth, as well as Indra and others, are established in their respective directions.
May the beings be satisfied with joyful minds; may they accept this bali offering.
Whether in a city, in battle, in the forest, or on the bank of a river.
In ponds, wells, trees, cremation grounds, and at crossroads.
Those who assume various forms and those who assume many forms.
"May they all be well-pleased and always accept my offering. Thus one should offer a handful of flowers.
The principal offering.

In front of the deity, on the ground, having placed a vessel containing food and side-dishes along with a *bindu*, a triangle, a circle, and a hexagon drawn with vermilion (*sindūra*), and having offered the *bali* while reciting: "Oṃ [mūla-mantra] obeisance to the substance for the *durgā*-bali," and having worshipped it with sandalwood paste and flowers using the root mantra, [one worships] the Root [Mantra] together with its limbs and weapons.

Having worshipped with the mantra: "Obeisance to the Goddess Caṇḍikā, who consists of the three qualities (triguṇātmikā), accompanied by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra, together with her vehicle, her retinue, and her power," and having presented the sacrificial offering (bali), [one recites] the root mantra: "Come, come, O Mother of the worlds! Accept this offering of meat and food; grant me success; destroy my enemies!"

*Hrīṃ hrīṃ huṃ phaṭ svāhā*. This is the *bali* offering to the venerable Goddess Durgā, who is endowed with her limbs (*sāṅgā*), weapons (*sāyudhā*), vehicle (*savāhanā*), retinue (*saparivārā*), and powers (*saśaktikā*), accompanied by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra, and whose nature consists of the three *guṇas*. Thus, one should offer the *bali* with the left thumb and ring finger. (The right hand is used for the ritual.)
One should abandon water with the hand.
Prayer: Oṃ! O supreme refuge for those who have come for protection, the wretched, and the afflicted!
O Goddess Nārāyaṇī, who removes the suffering of all! Salutations be unto you!

1. This is the lion *bali* mantra from the *Śāradā-tantra*: *Oṃ vajranakhadaṃṣṭrāyudhāya siṃhāya huṃ phaṭ namaḥ*. 2. *Oṃ sauṃ vanaspati-putrāya siṃhāya imaṃ baliṃ gṛhṇa 2 svāhā*. The buffalo *bali* mantra: *Oṃ bhūṃ mahiṣaśṛṅgebhyo mahiṣebhyaḥ imaṃ...* [gṛhṇa 2 svāhā].
Accept the offering, accept [it] twice! Svāhā! This is the mantra for the buffalo offering.

Oṃ, salutations to all the deities of the bali offering. Having thus worshipped everything, one should meditate upon the Kuṇḍalinī Śakti, whose nature is like a lotus fiber, having the form of a sleeping serpent, endowed with three and a half coils,
and encircling the Svayambhū-liṅga by joining mouth to mouth.

"Having the radiance of a mass of fire, suns, and lightning, and whose form is consciousness"—thus it is said in another Tantra. Having bound the *nārāca* mudrā: "O deities of the offering, being satisfied by this offering, please grant us forgiveness."

May the excellent ones, beginning with Vaṭuka, all the gods who bestow every accomplishment, grant [this] as they please and according to their will; O Maheśvarī, by your grace, may they grant peace and nourishment.

Having offered praise and released the mudrā, one should sprinkle oneself with water from the *prokṣaṇī* vessel. Thus [one should offer] the bali-offering to the five great elements (*pañcamahābhūta*). The mantras for that are as follows:
Those who are fierce, performers of fierce deeds, and dwellers in fierce abodes; the Mothers of terrible form, and those who are lords of the Gaṇas. (1)
May those who move on the earth, those who move in the sky, and likewise those who move in the intermediate space—
all of them, with delighted minds, accept this bali offering.
With these two mantras, one should offer an oblation (*bali*) of black gram and rice (*māṣabhakta*) in the ten directions outside.
Then, having sprinkled with the water of the *arghya* using the fingers of the left hand and having taken a handful of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*), [one should recite]: "Oṃ!
Whatever beings dwell here upon the surface of the earth, having accepted this oblation offered according to the rite..."
"May they all attain contentment; may they forgive me for anything else—salutations to them!
Having thus offered a handful of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*), having prostrated, and having washed his hands and feet, he should perform the ritual sipping of water (*ācamana*).
This is the "Piercing of the Field" (*kṣetrakīlana*).
131) Now, the method for the worship of the yantra.
In the center (of the principal yantra), having meditated upon the form [of the deity] by means of the root mantra atop the corpse-seat situated on the wheel,
and having visualized oneself in the form of the Kāmakalā, one should take the flowers and other offerings with the "tortoise-hand" gesture.
The ritual procedure for the worship of the yantra.

Then, on the lotus petals within the circle, O Goddess of gods, one should worship in sequence by moving counter-clockwise, beginning from the foremost petal; one should worship the deities of the limbs (aṅgadevatās) according to the very sequence prescribed in one's own ritual manual (kalpa).
From the *mūlādhāra*, one should meditate upon the Kuṇḍalinī— the power (*śakti*) of Kuṇḍalinī—
resembling a fiber of lotus-stalk, encircling the self-arisen liṅga (*svayambhūliṅga*), and possessing a luster like that of fire, the moon, the sun, and a mass of lightning.

[She who is of the nature of consciousness. Thus it is stated in another Tantra. Having visualized her situated at the head along the path of the *brahmarandhra*, and having brought down the Goddess—who has become merged with the nectar located there—into the red eight-petalled lotus situated at the heart, one should meditate upon her. [A sword, a discus, a mace, arrows, a bow, and a club... [a sword, a discus, a mace, arrows...]

I worship Mahākālī, who holds a bow, an iron club, a trident, a *bhuśuṇḍī* weapon, a severed head, and a conch in her hands; she has three eyes, is adorned with ornaments on all her limbs, possesses the luster of a blue sapphire, and has ten faces and ten feet— she whom the lotus-born Brahmā praised while Hari was asleep, so that he might slay Madhu.
[The *kaṭabha* || 1 ||] She who holds in her hands a rosary of seeds (*akṣasraj*), a battle-axe, a mace, an arrow,
a thunderbolt, a lotus, a bow, a water-pot (*kuṇḍikā*), a staff, a spear, a sword, a shield, a conch, a bell, a vessel of wine,
a trident, a noose, and the *sudarśana* discus— she whose face is serene.
[I worship] here Mahālakṣmī, the destroyer of the demon Bhaṇḍa, seated upon a lotus, together with Śiva and her attendants. || 2 ||

Having meditated in sequence on "the bell and the trident," and so forth, one should project the seed-syllable *yam* through the left nostril onto the flower in the hand. [Recite] the root mantra: "O Goddess of Gods!
"O Goddess, who are easily accessible to devotees and accompanied by your retinue! As long as I worship you, please remain here.
Reciting this mantra, one should place a flower upon the prepared image or the yantra.
The invocation. [The definition of the nārāca mudrā.]
If the tip of the thumb touches the tip of the middle finger while the other fingers remain unjoined, that shall be the mudrā of the supreme weapon named Nārāca, the destroyer of elemental beings.
[For the invocation and dismissal in an image, in water, or in fire, the root mantra is: Oṃ.

O Supreme Goddess! I invoke you—who abide within the self, unborn, and pure—into this physical form, just as one brings the portion of the oblation from the forest fire. Oṃ! I invoke you, Great Goddess, from the summit of the White Mountain, or from the solar orb, or even from the deep cavern of the heart-lotus.
The characteristics of the invocation mudrā (āvāhana-mudrā). || 1 ||
With hands joined in *añjali*, he offered flowers that had been properly honored.
This is declared as the *āvāhanī* (invocation) mudrā by the most excellent masters of the mudrās.
The añjali mudrā is described as having the tips of the thumbs joined at the base of the ring fingers.
And this is the mudrā known as the invocation, which serves to summon the Goddess.
In the *Tāpanīya* [Upaniṣad] of Rāma-pūrva.
The form of this deity is adorned by the nine-syllable mantra: *aiṃ hrīṃ klīṃ cāmuṇḍāyai vicce*. If worship is performed without a yantra, the deity does not become pleased.
In the Saṃhitā.
They say that the yantra consists of mantra, and the deity has the form of mantra;
a god worshipped by means of a yantra alone does not quickly become propitious.
For all mantras as well, worship upon the yantra is praised;
[as is] its installation. (p. 134)
(Original Text) Oṃ! This is your form of majesty; in it you are all-pervading, O Auspicious One.
Drawn by the oil of devotion, I establish [you] here like a lamp. (2)
Having thus established [the deity], [this is] the characteristic of the *sthāpana* mudrā.
With the life-force turned downward, it is called the *sthāpanī* [mudrā];
having established [the deity] with this *sthāpanī* mudrā.
The seat.
(Root Text) Oṃ! O Goddess, inner ruler of all! I prepare for you this auspicious seat, consisting of all seed-syllables, supreme, pure, and abiding within one's own self. || 3 ||
Please accept this seat; homage.
O Goddess, you whose nature is the Imperishable, seated comfortably upon this excellent throne!
O you who are established in auspiciousness! Be gracious, O Supreme Goddess!
"Upaviṣṭābhava" (Be seated), "Namaḥ" (Salutation). Having brought [the deity] into presence:
Oṃ! O Mistress of the Gods, O Excellent One! This power of form is none other than you.
O you who are intent on bestowing grace upon your devotees, please manifest your presence within that [image]. || 4 ||
With both fists joined together and the pair of thumbs raised upward,
this mudrā is prescribed by those learned in the Tantras for the purpose of invoking the presence [of the deity].
The complete cessation.
(Root Text) Oṃ! By your command, O Goddess of gods, O ocean of mercy, O ocean of virtues, O fatherly Guru, I restrain you who are solely satisfied with the bliss of the Self. 5.
Thus, having completely restrained [the breath]. This is the characteristic of the *sannirodhana* mudrā.
That very [power], containing the thumb within, is proclaimed as "Sannirodhā."
Bringing [the object] face-to-face.
(Root Text) Oṃ! Whatever task may have been left incomplete due to ignorance, mental distress, distraction, or deficiency in the means—be present even for that. 6.
Having thus brought [it] face-to-face, it is the *sammukhī-mudrā*.
The binding of the hands in añjali at the heart is the mudrā of prayer.
The ritual of sakalīkaraṇa.
O Maheśvarī! Filling the sacrificial altar with Your glance that showers nectar, remain present in embodied form for the completion of the sacrifice. (7)
The mudrā of sakalīkaraṇa.
The placement of the six limbs upon the limbs of the deity constitutes the rite of sakalīkaraṇa (the act of making complete).
Alternatively, there is another mudrā for the ritual of sakalīkaraṇa.

The ritual placement (vinyāsa) of the mantras beginning with the Heart-mantra upon the body from the heart to its extremities, and upon the fingers beginning with the little finger, is considered to be the act of "making complete" (sakalīkaraṇa).
The veil.
(Root Text) Oṃ! O you whose splendor blazes forth beyond the reach of speech, mind, sight, and hearing!
Be quickly enveloped on all sides by a mass of your own radiance! 8.
The Avaguṇṭhana mudrā.
With the left hand formed into a fist and the index finger extended downward,
this is the *avaguṇṭhana* (veiling) mudrā when it is rotated all around.
Having veiled [the deity] with "Bhagavati Hūṃ," one should perform the binding of the directions with a snap of the fingers. This is the rite of nectarization (*amṛtīkaraṇa*).
The most excellent of teachers should perform the rite of immortalization (amṛtīkaraṇa) with that [substance].
The Dhenu-mudrā is the Amṛtī-mudrā.
With the little fingers and ring fingers again joined face-to-face,
and likewise the index and middle fingers, this is proclaimed as the Dhenu Mudrā.
Then, having rendered [the substance] nectar-like by means of the *dhenumudrā*, having rendered it supreme by means of the *paramīkaraṇamudrā*,
and forming the *mahāmudrā*.
The characteristics of Mahāmudrā.
With the thumbs interlocked and the fingers of the hands extended,
this is declared by the wise to be the Mahāmudrā, which effects supreme transformation.
One should offer a welcome.
(Root Text) Oṃ! To her whose vision the gods desire for the sake of attaining their own cherished goals—to that Supreme Goddess, welcome, welcome to you! 11.
"One should perform it with that," so it has been declared by those expert in the scriptures of mantra.
Welcome; all is well.
(Root Text) Oṃ! My purpose is accomplished; I have been graced by you. My entire life has become meaningful, O Goddess, Sovereign of Gods! Welcome once again to you. 12.
A hearty welcome! Please be seated on a seat. Here is water for washing the feet.
Water mixed with śyāmāka, viṣṇukrāntā, lotus, and dūrvā grass is for the purpose of the water for washing the feet (pādya).
(Verse 13) Oṃ! To those lotus feet of Yours, which possess a form of supreme bliss through contact with even a fragment of devotion, I offer this pure water for washing the feet.
Thus is the water for the feet; [then] the water for sipping.
Having cast lavanga, jāti, and kakkola into the water for sipping (ācamanīya).
Oṃ! To her who is the object of knowledge even for the Vedas, the divine essence of the gods—O Sovereign!
I offer this water for sipping, the cause of purification for those already pure. (14)
The water for sipping (ācamana) and the materials for the *svadhā* offering are the items for the *arghya*.

One should place dūrvā grass, sesame seeds, barley, the tips of *darbha* grass, mustard seeds, barley, flowers, and unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*), along with fragrance, into the *arghya* vessel; with that, one should perform the *arghya* offering upon the head.
The water of honor (arghya).
(Root Text) Oṃ, I offer this arghya to you—divine, the remover of the threefold affliction, characterized by supreme bliss, and itself liberated from the threefold affliction. Svāhā! 15.
Thus [is offered] the arghya upon the head; [followed by] the madhuparka.
Into the vessel for the madhuparka, one should pour curd, clarified butter, and honey.
(mū0) Oṃ! To you who are free from all impurity, O bestower of perfect bliss!
O Goddess, I offer this madhuparka; may it be efficacious for me. || 16 ||
Having thus placed it in the mouth.
Thus [is the ritual for] the honey-mixture (madhuparka). [Then follows] the sipping of water (ācamana).
(Verse 17) Oṃ! Even one who is impure or defiled by remnants of food attains purification merely by the remembrance of You; to You, therefore, is this water for sipping offered again.
Sugandhitaitra-tailam (Root Text): Oṃ! O Mistress of the World, O Treasure of Compassion, accept this oil with its essence through your own essence!
O pure-souled one! I bestow supreme affection upon all worlds.
Anointing with fragrant unguents.
(Root Text) Oṃ. Having rubbed him with turmeric and other substances, one should bathe him while reciting both [mantras]:
various fragrant materials, sandalwood, and turmeric combined.
"I have brought an ointment for your bath; please accept it. (19)
"O Bhagavatī Caṇḍikā, I offer this unguent; salutations!
There is no fault in rubbing the deity with the thumbs. In another tantra it is said:
"One should not rub the deity with the thumbs, nor should one worship [the deity] with flowers placed below."
One should not throw water with the tips of kuśa grass; it would be like the falling of a thunderbolt. || 20 ||

[Clarified butter, milk, water, sugar, and honey combined—each weighing one *pala*—are known as the "five nectars" (*pañcāmṛta*). This is the ritual bath with the five nectars (*pañcāmṛta-snāna*). Regarding the measure of the five nectars, it is stated in the *Yāmala*:
The milk bath.
(Verse 21) Oṃ! This milk, produced from the wish-fulfilling cow, is the supreme sustenance for all, purifying, and the cause of sacrifice; it is offered for the purpose of bathing.
Having bathed again with pure water, [one performs] the curd-bath.
(Verse 22) Oṃ! This curd, produced from milk, sweet and sour, and possessing the luster of the moon, has been brought by me, O Goddess; please accept it for the purpose of bathing.
Again, having bathed [the image] with pure water, [perform] the ghee-bath (ghṛtasnāna).
(Root Text) Oṃ. I shall offer to you ghee produced from fresh butter, which brings satisfaction to all; please accept it for the purpose of bathing. || 23 ||
Having bathed again with pure water, [this is] the honey-bath.
(Verse 24) Oṃ! This honey, produced from the blossoms of trees, delicious and sweet, divine, bestowing energy and nourishment—please accept it for the purpose of bathing.
Having bathed again with pure water, [there follows] the sugar-bath.
(Verse 25) Oṃ! This divine sugar-candy, produced from the essence of sugarcane, which bestows nourishment and removes impurities, is accepted for the purpose of bathing.
Having bathed [the deity] again with pure water, one performs the bathing with the five nectars by combining them into one.
(Verse 26) Oṃ! May you accept this five-fold nectar (pañcāmṛta)—consisting of milk, curd, ghee, honey, and sugar—brought by me for the purpose of bathing.
Having bathed [the image] again with pure water, [perform] the sandalwood (scented) bath.
(Original Text) Oṃ! O Goddess, Queen of the Gods! Please accept this sandalwood, produced on the Malaya mountain and originating from *agaru* [black aloe], for the purpose of bathing. || 27 ||
Having bathed again with pure water, this is the ritual bath with its constituent parts.
(Root Text) Oṃ! O Sovereign! I offer this bath, complete with its limbs and sub-limbs, to You whose own form is immersed in the ocean of supreme bliss and awakening. 28.
I offer a bath for all the limbs; obeisance. [The Consecration: [Note:
With the exception of Śiva and Sūrya, one should perform the Great Consecration everywhere using only a conch shell.
(Root Text) Oṃ, then with a thousand conch shells, or a hundred, or even according to one's capacity.
While recollecting the mantra, one should consecrate the Goddess with waters mixed with perfumes.
Again, water for sipping.
It is likewise prescribed at the conclusion of bathing, clothing, and the sacred thread, as well as at the end of the food offering (naivedya).
Clothing: [It should be yellow for Viṣṇu, white for Śambhu, and red for Vighna, Arka, and Śakti.
One should discard clothing that is torn, dirty, worn out, or defiled by oil and the like.]
From [a vessel] defiled by oil and the like, disease arises; from one with a hole, there will be censure.
From old age comes poverty; from impurity comes the loss of luster.
Oṃ! To You whose own secret splendor is veiled by the variegated cloth of *māyā*, I prepare a garment of unobstructed consciousness. (30)
An upper garment.
(Verse 31) Oṃ! To you, that Supreme Goddess, depending upon whom Mahāmāyā always deludes the world, I offer this upper garment.
The sacred thread.
(Verse 32) Oṃ! To you, whose threefold power this entire universe is woven together, I offer this sacred thread as a sacrificial cord.
The sipping of water (ācamana). The ornaments (ābhūṣaṇa).
Oṃ! O you whose limbs are naturally beautiful, who are the refuge of various gods, and who are worshipped by the immortals—I fashion these diverse ornaments for you. 33.
The deluder of the world.
One should place each individual letter of the Mātṛkā, encased by the root mantra, upon the limbs of the deity; this yoga is the deluder of the world.
Fragrance.
(Verse 34) Oṃ! O Supreme Goddess, who fills the quarters of space with the excellence of supreme bliss, please graciously accept this supreme fragrance.
The fragrance mudrā.
One should display the fragrance mudrā by joining the little finger and the thumb.
And I offer substances of various fragrances and auspicious qualities; obeisance! || 36 ||
Unbroken [grains].
O Supreme Goddess! These unbroken grains, smeared with saffron and beautifully adorned, have been offered by me with devotion; please accept them, O Parameśvarī. (37)
Flowers.
"Let this supreme flower, born from the fourth forest, enchanting with its various qualities and possessing intense fragrance, be accepted. (38)
One should display the flower mudrā by joining the index finger and the thumb;
[this refers to] flowers produced during their respective seasons.
With *sevantikā*, *vakula*, *campaka*, *pāṭala*, and *abja* flowers; with *punnāga*, *jāti*, *karavīra*, and *rasāla* blossoms. (39)
O Sovereign of the Universe! I worship you with bilva sprouts, tulasī leaves, and mālatī flowers; be gracious unto me. (40)
The fragrance of other flowers should extend as far as the sacrificial area;
likewise, one should prepare flowers, the five products of the cow (pañcagavya), and other ritual offerings.
O Goddess of the gods! Having smelled it and offered it, a man shall fall into hell.
That which has been touched by a limb, smelled, or has become stale should be discarded by the wise.
One should discard flowers that are infested with hair or insects, those that are withered or stale, those that have fallen off on their own, and those that are otherwise defiled.
Flowers to be avoided in the worship of the Goddess.

In the month of Śakva (Mārgaśīrṣa), [one should offer] dūrvā grass, arka, mandāra, mālūra, and atigara; in the month of Ravi (Sūrya—Jyeṣ� scentless flowers, those defiled by hair or insects, and those with a pungent odor. || 41 ||
